16	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
17	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
18	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
19	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
20	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
21	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
22	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
23	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
24	- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
25	- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
26	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's phone call plus emailed Word nomination with a structured feed into HPL scheduling that rolls forward and is sent only when volumes change.. Why: The 16 minutes a day rest on steps the mail does not show: a phone call every day (only 5 of about 23 nominations mention one), HPL retyping the Word file (no message shows it), and frequent no-change days (none shown; REVISED resends and monthly nominations show volumes change), and the 30-a-month rate ignores that weekend days come in one Friday email (1330.eml); three critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the schedulers (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) showing what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as retyping it into the system, keying errors, corrections or rework after revisions, and nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller saving counted once per working day.
27	- Hourly generator checkout calls to BPA (Grays Harbor and Frontier): Meter the two generators automatically so their hourly output goes to BPA without a trader phoning it in.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA' ($3,102.50 a month), citing the same messages 357.eml and 506.eml.
28	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only valuation view with back-dated curves so it can produce counterparties' audit MTM valuations itself, without going to the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
29	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off tiny Strangers Gas volumes under a standing approval and send the rest to Daren Farmer as one weekly electronic list instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of 1999-2000 flows sent mostly in a burst from 11 Dec 2000 to 12 Jan 2001 and none appear after that, though the mailbox runs to late 2001; so the work is an episode that has ended, not 10 items a month, and the same work has already been rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, in this or other mailboxes (Cernosek, Lannou, Boas), that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
30	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a counterparty valuation report with stored year-end and month-end curves, so they can answer audit requests without going to the desks.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2, $1,381.25 a month), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241.
31	- Daily hand-forwarding of Credit's Credit Report: Put the book administrators who rebook the deals (Carole Frank and others) on Credit's Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 3, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards to Carole Frank in giron-d/sent.
32	- Flipping ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books: Have EOL/TAGG book deals with ECC's master-swap counterparties straight to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book, with a daily exception report, instead of manual search-and-flip requests.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals', which cites the same Giron messages.
33	- Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report: Put the West desk's rebook handler (Carole Frank) or a desk mailbox directly on Credit's daily Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every business day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 4, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards in giron-d/sent.
34	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a back-dated counterparty MTM report so the desks no longer run and redact a mini-book for each auditor request.. Why: This work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2, $1,381.25 a month), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241.
35	- Monthly sweep of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals before NYMEX close: Book ECC counterparty deals into the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book automatically, and run a report that lists any that slip through, instead of a monthly manual sweep and email chain.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as decisions.md item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' ($364.65 a month), which cites six of the same eight Giron messages (114, 195, 360, 407, 535, 550).
36	- Monthly flip of ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books before NYMEX invoicing: Extend the EOL auto-booking program to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties and run a nightly TAGG exception query for misbooked ENA deals, replacing the monthly all-books sweep.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' ($364.65 a month), which cites the same Giron messages (108, 114, 195, 292, 360, 407) and already books every ECC counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically with a daily list of deals that slip through.
37	- Weekly California Capacity Report: Generate the Friday California Capacity Report automatically from TW and El Paso flow postings and Gas Daily/EOL prices, so Michelle Lokay only checks it before sending.. Why: Another critic saved the same work with essentially the same change while this one was being checked ('Weekly California Capacity Report', decisions.md Saved item 5, $88.40 a month), and it cites the same lokay-m report messages.
38	- Weekly Transwestern California Capacity Report: Generate the weekly California Capacity Report automatically from flow and price data, so Michelle Lokay only reviews it before it goes out.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Weekly California Capacity Report' (item 5 in decisions.md), which cites the same lokay-m messages. The proposal also says the report is 'retyped from scratch', but sent_items/47.eml shows it is made by forwarding last week's email and typing over it.

Group,
A quick note regarding Pace transmission reservations on their oasis sites.  We have recently paid PACE $57,000 for transmission in May that we reserved but did not flow.  PACE says that their transmission is on a take or pay basis.  My contention is that we may have reserved the transmission, but then attempted to remove it immediately (wrong hour, wrong mw value on the submission etc.) and were unable to, or were told by the dispatcher that the dispatcher would take care of it.   Then nothing happens.  There are two things we need to do to prevent this.

	One: Submit our transactions correctly the first time.  Then withdraw them immediately through the Pacificorp Oasis system if there is a problem.

	Two: Send me an email each time the dispatchers remove requests on our behalf, or if We/PAC are/is unable to take the request out of their computer system.

Hopefully, this will prevent the extra charges, or give us a means to pull tapes and contest the charges.

Thanks for your help in limiting these egregious expenses

Bill

	ryan.slinger@enron.com, geir.solberg@enron.com, kate.symes@enron.com, 
	bill.williams@enron.com
Subject: EOL Deal entry and status update.
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
X-From: Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=BWILLIA5>
X-To: Anderson, John </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Janders3>, Bland, Todd <Todd.Bland@ENRON.com>, Dean, Craig <Craig.Dean@ENRON.com>, Guzman, Mark </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mguzman3>, Harasin, Leaf </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Lharasin>, Linder, Eric </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Elinder>, Merriss, Steven </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Smerris>, Meyers, Bert </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bmeyers>, Mier, Michael </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mmier>, Porter, David V. </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Dporter3>, Presto, Darin </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Dpresto2>, Slinger, Ryan </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Rslinger>, Solberg, Geir </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Gsolber>, Symes, Kate </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Ksymes>, Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bwillia5>
X-cc: 
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \ExMerge - Williams III, Bill\Sent Items
X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
X-FileName: 

Group,

We are continuing to refine our deal entry techniques and spreadsheet techniques. We are having great success with EOL so far. For further clarification.
	


	1. ALL DEALS UNDER ST-WHOURLY--except a lending/parking deal or cut. For example if we are lending with ST-SW and we buy for them in NP-15. The buy in NP-15 is under ST-WHOURLY, the EPMICALPOOL Buy/Resale from NP-15 to FC345 is under ST-WHOURLY, the INTER-DESK sale is made under ST-WHOURLY (at the end of the day--see #3), and the sale to EPE is under ST-SW. The export in CAPS is also under ST-SW.

	2. ONE DEAL FOR AN ON-PEAK or OFF-PEAK PURCHASE or SALE.--For example one deal for a sale to the imbalance, one deal for a sale to EPE

	3. ONE DEAL FOR AN INTER-DESK SALE or PURCHASE--done by the NIGHT SHIFT at the weighted average price for the entire strip, transmission costs should be included. We are just averaging the purchase price or sale price for specific deals. (see ST-WBOM SP-15 section of AUG TRADING sheet on 08/29/01 for an example)

	4. INC SHEETS MUST BE MAINTAINED, DEALS ENTERED AND ROUTED EACH HOUR--only way to stay ahead

	5. WE ARE GENERATING SIGNIFICANTLY MORE REVENUE AND PROFIT TRADING WITH EOL (over $130,000 in the last 5 days alone--does not include congestion revenue!)--530+ trades, 13,100 extra mws traded with EOL in 8 days.

	6. MEETING ON TUESDAY 09/04 at 4PM


Finally, I will be out of the office for Friday and will be in Seattle through Sunday. You should be able to reach me on my cell phone (503) 887-3449. If you can not reach me, please refer questions regarding trading to Ryan Slinger, (503) 789-1306.

Thanks for the continued hard work and attention to detail,

Bill

Subject:	FSP Milestone Complete

Good Afternoon,

I am pleased to announce that we have finally completed the 10 day parallel test milestone for FSP.  We were also seeing solid performance for our key metrics during the parallel (template writing 1:30 - 2:30, finals processing 5-7 minutes).  Lastly, based on my understanding of our go-live bet, my total debt owed to Tim Belden = $13.00.  Tim, I gave the money to Debra.

What Next?

User Training
I will be working with the DA & Real time guys to make sure everyone is up-to-speed with the new system.  We are also in the process of developing some user documentation cheat sheets to help in the transition.

Production Parallel
We have already begun using FSP in parallel in production by writing templates in FSP & comparing them to CAPS.  We will continue doing this until we are getting consistent results between the two systems.  This production parallel has necessitated some changes to the existing Enpower_to_CAPS report that we have already started modifying.

How long? 

Once bit, twice shy.  No money on this one, but I don't think it should take over a week to train the users.  The production parallel may take a little longer.  I am really relying on the users to wrap this one up.  Kysa Alport has already volunteered for this duty and I spent a good part of today training her.  

Thanks,  David Poston

259	- Manual monthly reconciliation of the full-month position (scheduled vs. actual volumes by nomination and meter). Daren Farmer sends the whole HPL position to the team, and each person has to pick out their own meters by hand and confirm back to him by a deadline (close of business Thursday).: The message is titled 'Full month position', which suggests a recurring month-end job. It has about 3,600 nomination rows with SCHEDULED/ACTUAL/VARIANCE/STATUS/METER columns. Recipients are asked to 'pull your own meters out of this and confirm back to me', which is manual filtering and confirming that could be automated: split the report by meter owner and flag variances. Many rows show large variances and PENDING status, which may each need follow-up. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3221.eml
260	- Workaround when report attachments fail: large position spreadsheets get pasted into the email body because the attachment 'keeps bouncing off the gateway'.: The phrase 'keeps bouncing' suggests the failure has happened more than once. It costs repeated send attempts, and pasting the data makes it harder to filter or reuse. A shared report location or report system would remove the email handoff altogether. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3221.eml
261	- Data quality checks on the scheduling/position report. FLOW_DATE values in a 'full month' report cover all of 2001 in day/month format, and counterparty IDs repeat (TXU-0000 to TXU-0399 cycle over and over).: A month-end position that spans dates across the whole year suggests the extract is wrong or unfiltered. Each recipient would then have to clean or check the data by hand before confirming. Investigators should look for other messages about bad position or nomination reports from the same group (Farmer, Giron, Williams, Lokay). Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3221.eml
262	- Shippers email Transwestern to change a contract (raise MDQ for one or two days, extend the term, assign receipt points, continue last month's terms). The account director replies 'Approved' and forwards each request to Dennis Lee or Michael Bodnar, who draft an amendment and update the admin contract.: Julie Reames at BR sent same-day 'increase contract 27748' requests on 12/10, 12/10 (for 12/11), 12/11 and 12/13. The same pattern shows up with Western Gas, TMV, Reliant and PPL. Each one is a phone call, then an email, then a forward, then a manual amendment. Some are re-forwarded as FYI, and PPL needed several amendments (#3, #4) with mix-ups over which version was signed. In reviewing some of the imbalance numbers, I discovered that Valero Texoma 
(#71) BAV volumes have not fed into POPS since 3/14 causing an out of balance 
at the meter in excess of 500,000mm month to date.  The more critical part of 
this problem, however, is that POPS has fed 0 volumes back to Sitara on some 
of the HPLC deals.  This means that these purchase volumes (expenses) have 
not been picked up in Tom's P&L and are, instead, sitting in UA4.  To the 
extent that the purchase prices vary from the UA4 value, the P&L may take a 
hit when these actual volumes flow through.

I realize that Kim is out and that you guys are stretched thin, however, a 
problem of this magnitude needs to be addressed as soon as it's discovered.  
Someone needs to be overriding the 0 volumes so that Sitara is receiving 
correct information and the P&L is kept as accurate as possible.

Please give me a call if you have any questions.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. Some of the idea may be sound, but the evidence can't support it as written.

**Why it failed**

1. **It counts the same messages as a saved item.** The eight Credit Reports cited for the rebook lines are all forwards that saved item 6, "Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report", already cites. Rebooking deals is different work from Giron forwarding the report. But the only proof that it happens every day is those same forwards, and the check refused to save it for that reason. Only a few messages show rebooking on its own: `351.eml` (Bank of America, with Giron replying "Done"), `116.eml`/`117.eml` (W&T Offshore) and `124.eml`. Counted from the eight reports themselves, the work happens about 1.75 times a month, which is about $45 a month, not $714.

2. **Several claims are overstated or wrong.**
   - "The root cause behind the daily Credit Report" is not true. The report also lists credit holds ("Pending ..."), "Need L/C" wording for confirms, and moves from ENA to ECC under the ISDA.
   - "The same wrong names come back day after day" is not true either. They come back weeks apart: Louis Dreyfus in 4 of the 8 reports, Bank of America in 3, and most other names in 2 at most.
   - The "half are repeats" assumption is too high. I counted the rebook lines in the eight reports and about 25 of 58 (roughly 40%) repeat a name already corrected.
   - Some quotes are in the wrong file. The Virginia Power line quoted is in `153.eml`; `151.eml` has a different deal (qW9572.1). The PanCanadian deal qX4599.1 is only in `149.eml`; `263.eml` has qO1735.1. The AEP line in `263.eml` is "AEP Communications", not "AEP Energy Services Ltd".

3. **Switching names automatically would put deals under the wrong company.** The right company for the same name changes:
   - The Louis Dreyfus Holdings deals were rebooked to "Louis Dreyfus Corporation" in 263, 151 and 149, but to "Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp" in 154.
   - Aquila and Utilicorp were corrected in opposite directions: Aquila to Utilicorp in January (263), Utilicorp to Aquila Risk Management in March and April (149, 75).
   - In `149.eml`, deals already under "AEP Energy Services, Inc." are rebooked to "AEP Energy Services, Inc.", so the problem there isn't the name picked at all.

   At most, the change could warn the person entering the deal and let them confirm.

**What could fix it**

This is mainly a problem of evidence, not of the idea. The fix needs messages that show rebooking separately from Giron's forwards. Look in the mailboxes of the book administrators and Credit staff (Carole Frank, Derek Bailey, Julie Brewer, Lesli Campbell, Russell Diamond) for rebook requests and "Done" replies, or for any message saying how many deals are rebooked each day or week. A warning-only proposal built on that could then be judged on its own.

Files are in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2\proposals\`:
- `credit-report-rebook-aliases.json` (my rewritten proposal, which failed the check)
- `credit-report-rebook-aliases-reject.json` (the recorded rejection)

content.text: Two assistants forward vendor reports by hand every day. The Energy Market Report goes out on consecutive business days. Sending this one to the critic.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Deliver the daily vendor "Energy Market Report" straight to a West Power distribution list instead of an assistant hand-forwarding it every business day

TODAY: The Energy Market Report (a vendor price report with a PDF and in-body Western price tables) arrives in Jill Chatterton's mailbox. Every business day she forwards it ("FW: Energy Market Report - <date>") to the same 12 individually addressed West Power traders (Alonso, Badeer, Belden, Crandall, Driscoll, Fischer, Mallory, Motley, Richter, Scholtes, Swerzbin, Bill Williams III).
- corpus/williams-w3/inbox/86.eml (29 Jan 2002): "Subject: FW: Energy Market Report - 1/28/02", from jill.chatterton@enron.com to the 12 traders. The body is the vendor's report: "Energy Market Report / Monday, January 28, 2002 / *See attached pdf file." and "Western Pre-Scheduled Firm Electricity Prices($/MWh)".
- The same forward on consecutive business days: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/75.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 01/29/02"), 62.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 01/30/02"), 57.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 01/31/02"), 49.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 02/01/02"), 35.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 02/04/02"), 23.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 02/05/02"). That is seven business days in a row, 1/28 to 2/5 with the weekend skipped, so it is a daily task.
- The list is maintained by hand. A similar daily vendor PDF forward by another assistant, Theresa Villeggiante (Gas Daily / Power Daily PDFs), shows recipients being added only on request: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/7.eml (Bill Williams III, 31 Jan 2002): "Could you add DL-Portland Shift to this distribution. I would like the guys in Real-Time to be able to see this information when they come in." Her reply in corpus/williams-w3/inbox/67.eml: "No problem, is it possible for you to give me a list of names as I am not sure who does what just yet."

WHERE IT STALLS: traders get the report only when the assistant is at her desk to forward it, and adding a reader takes an email exchange.

CHANGE: Have the vendor's delivery address be a distribution list (e.g., DL-West Power Market Reports), or set a mail rule that auto-forwards the report on arrival. The trading desk owns the list membership.

AFTERWARDS: The report reaches traders on arrival with no assistant step. Adding a reader is a one-time list change.

ESTIMATE: Per forward, opening, forwarding and addressing 12 named recipients takes about 3 min of assistant time. Frequency is every business day (the seven consecutive dated forwards above), about 21 a month. 21 × 3 = 63 min ≈ 1.05 h/month × $85 ≈ $89/month. I count only the Energy Market Report forward. The Gas Daily/Power Daily forward in 7.eml/67.eml is likely daily too (date-stamped file names "gasdaily.01.31.2002.pdf"), but only one instance is in the archive, so I don't claim savings for it. List-maintenance emails are also left out.

Every business day she forwards it ("FW: Energy Market Report - <date>") to the same 12 individually addressed West Power traders (Alonso, Badeer, Belden, Crandall, Driscoll, Fischer, Mallory, Motley, Richter, Scholtes, Swerzbin, Bill Williams III).
- corpus/williams-w3/inbox/86.eml (29 Jan 2002): "Subject: FW: Energy Market Report - 1/28/02", from jill.chatterton@enron.com to the 12 traders. The body is the vendor's report: "Energy Market Report / Monday, January 28, 2002 / *See attached pdf file." and "Western Pre-Scheduled Firm Electricity Prices($/MWh)".
- The same forward on consecutive business days: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/75.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 01/29/02"), 62.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 01/30/02"), 57.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 01/31/02"), 49.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 02/01/02"), 35.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 02/04/02"), 23.eml ("FW: Energy Market Report - 02/05/02"). That is seven business days in a row, 1/28 to 2/5 with the weekend skipped, so it is a daily task.
- The list is maintained by hand. A similar daily vendor PDF forward by another assistant, Theresa Villeggiante (Gas Daily / Power Daily PDFs), shows recipients being added only on request: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/7.eml (Bill Williams III, 31 Jan 2002): "Could you add DL-Portland Shift to this distribution. I would like the guys in Real-Time to be able to see this information when they come in." Her reply in corpus/williams-w3/inbox/67.eml: "No problem, is it possible for you to give me a list of names as I am not sure who does what just yet."

WHERE IT STALLS: traders get the report only when the assistant is at her desk to forward it, and adding a reader takes an email exchange.

CHANGE: Have the vendor's delivery address be a distribution list (e.g., DL-West Power Market Reports), or set a mail rule that auto-forwards the report on arrival. The trading desk owns the list membership.

AFTERWARDS: The report reaches traders on arrival with no assistant step. Adding a reader is a one-time list change.

ESTIMATE: Per forward, opening, forwarding and addressing 12 named recipients takes about 3 min of assistant time. Frequency is every business day (the seven consecutive dated forwards above), about 21 a month. 21 × 3 = 63 min ≈ 1.05 h/month × $85 ≈ $89/month. I count only the Energy Market Report forward. The Gas Daily/Power Daily forward in 7.eml/67.eml is likely daily too (date-stamped file names "gasdaily.01.31.2002.pdf"), but only one instance is in the archive, so I don't claim savings for it. List-maintenance emails are also left out.

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Brown, Elizabeth  
Sent:	Thursday, January 10, 2002 2:02 PM
To:	Mulligan, Amy; Hanagriff, Richard
Cc:	Lokay, Michelle
Subject:	FW: Transwestern Capacity Release - ENA/Burlington 
Importance:	High

FYI - When January 2002 invoices are run, please be advised that a manual adjustment will need to occur on ENA's contract 24924.  The deal was structured whereby TW would receive a marketing fee equal to 50% of the rate negotiated in excess of the original contracted rate between ENA and TW; the other 50% goes to ENA.

Here's the basics:
ENA's contract with TW is at a daily rate of $0.0600 (one-part)
The release to Burlington is at a daily rate of $0.0650 (demand only plus applicable commodity and fuel based on usage)
TW will bill Burlington through normal course of business (reservation of $34,125 [$0.0650 x 25,000 x 21days] plus applicable commodity fees)
ENA demand invoice will need to be adjusted so that they only receive a capacity release credit of $32,812.50  [($0.0650 - $0.0025) x 25,000 x 21days]
TW will need to book marketing fee revenues of $1,312.50 [$0.0025 x 25,000 x 21 days]  (Richard - do we need/have a separate account for these revenues??)

Michelle - I know you indicated that ENA is looking to get a payment of $1,312.50 for their portion of the incremental fee charged.  However, we will need to discuss further.  The invoice that will be generated to ENA will not represent a credit due them since we would still be billing them for the first 11 days prior to this release.  

We can discuss further when the billing cycle approaches.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

Elizabeth

I saved the proposal as item 15 in decisions.md. The pipeline values it at $8.50 a month, not the $89 you estimated.

**What checked out:** All seven forwards are in the mail (inbox/86, 75, 62, 57, 49, 35, 23). Each goes from Jill Chatterton to the same 12 traders, and the vendor report is passed on unchanged. The quotes about adding readers (sent_items/7.eml and inbox/67.eml) are accurate. Nothing in decisions.md covers the Energy Market Report, so this isn't a duplicate.

**What I changed:**
- **Minutes, 3 to 2.** Forwarding an unchanged email to names Outlook fills in as you type is closer to 2 minutes than 3.
- **Your "where it stalls" point is backed up.** Each forward goes out between about noon and 2:20 PM Pacific on the business day after the report's date. For example, the 1/28 report reached the traders at 12:18 PM on 29 Jan. I put this in the "today" field. I had to drop the message's Date line as a quote because the check only accepts words from the decoded message text.

**Why the figure is low:** No message says how often the report comes, so the pipeline worked out the rate from the dates: 7 forwards spread over January and February 2002 counts as 3 a month. Your figure assumed a real rate of about 21 a month, one every business day. That gives 2 minutes × 3 = 0.1 hours, or $8.50 a month. To raise it, you'd need a message that says outright how often the report comes, such as a vendor subscription notice or a "daily" mention. I searched these seven messages and found none.

file.content:
Group,

Cuts are on the way. While most can be zeroed out in Enpower (for LD's) like normal, longterm contracts will require an annuity for the value of the cut on that particular day. In the interest of being uniform, the guidelines for cuts are below. 

We will be handling cuts in the following manner:

1. Documentation is priority #1. We need to fill out a cut sheet with the times, the name of the person who called, the tag number, the quantity and price.

2. After attempting to resupply the cut or find an alternate sink we need to carefully document changes in the new enpower workspace.

3. We need to zero out all cut deals in Enpower, we then need to calculate the value of the deals and make an annuity. The annuity must be made HE 1 on the following day of the schedule. The annuity needs to be for 1 mw for the value of the zeroed out contract. In the comment section of the annuity you must include the Enpower deal # of the cut deal and should include an indication of the number of mws each hour and the contract price--for example (4 hours @ 25 mws X $100 per mw = $10,000).

4. Please be as accurate as possible. We still need to be flat in Enpower at the end of each day. And we still need to calculate our daily position.

5. Put all cut sheets in the accordion folder on Kate Symes' Desk.

I appreciate your help and diligence.
Thanks,

Bill

content.text: I'm drafting a proposal on the nightly schedule checkouts: about 27 named counterparties, and each confirmation save takes about a minute.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Cut the dead time in the Portland real-time desk's nightly counterparty checkouts. Pre-fill counterparty contact details and make the Enpower Path Confirmation save run in the background, one batch per counterparty.

TODAY: Every night between HE 19 and HE 21 the real-time shift calls each major marketer and utility to check out the next day's schedules. For each counterparty the trader highlights that counterparty's paths in the new Enpower Path Confirmation tool, clicks the phone icon, types the counterparty contact information into a pop-up, and waits about a minute while it saves to Enpower.
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/86.eml (Bill Williams III to DL-Portland Real Time Shift, 19 Nov 2001, "Checkouts"): "You must check out with all major marketers and utilities each night. This would include but not be limited to: AEP, AES-New Energy, Aquila, Avista, Calpine, Constellation, Coral, Duke, Dynegy, El Paso Merchant, Exelon, Meico, Mirant, Morgan, NCPA, Reliant, PPLMontana, PowerX, Sempra, SMUD, TransAlta, Williams, and southwest utilities such as Pinnacle West, SRP, PNM, PSCO and Pacificorp." (27 named) / "These checkouts should be started in HE 19 and finished by HE 21." / "Suggestion: Sort by counterparty while making confirmation calls. When all schedules with that counterparty are confirmed, highlight each schedule" / "Confirm a path by highlighting and clicking the telephone icon. A screen will come up requesting contact information from the appropriate counterparty. Because this information saves directly to Enpower, save time runs about a minute."
- The same message shows checkouts can be taken off the desk where another party already does them: "Northwest counterparties are checked out by BPA and do not need to be checked again by us (this would include SCL, TCL, PSPL, BPAP, GCPUD, EWEB, IPC, MPC, SNPD, WWP)."
WHERE IT STALLS: about a minute of waiting for each counterparty's save, plus retyping the same counterparty contact details every night, inside a 2-hour window that competes with live real-time trading.

CHANGE: (1) Keep a counterparty checkout-contact table in Enpower (desk name, phone, usual contact) and pre-fill the pop-up, so the trader edits only if the contact differs. (2) Have the Path Confirmation save write to Enpower asynchronously, or from a local queue, so the trader moves straight to the next counterparty instead of waiting about a minute.

AFTERWARDS: The calls themselves stay. Per counterparty the trader clicks confirm, accepts the pre-filled contact and moves on, about 10-15 seconds instead of about 2 minutes.

ESTIMATE: Per counterparty today, about 1 minute of save wait (stated in 86.eml) plus about 1 minute typing contact info = about 2 min. Afterwards about 0.25 min. Saving about 1.75 min × 27 named counterparties = about 47 min a night. I take a conservative 25 counterparties, since some may have no schedules some nights: 25 × 1.75 ≈ 44 min a night. The frequency is "each night", 30 nights a month: 44 × 30 = 1,320 min = 22 h/month × $85 ≈ $1,870/month. If you count only the stated 1-minute save wait (no contact-entry saving), it is 25 × ~0.9 min × 30 ≈ 11 h ≈ $955/month.

1	Message-ID: <21363001.1075839993610.JavaMail.evans@thyme>
2	Date: Mon, 19 Nov 2001 19:55:40 -0800 (PST)
3	From: bill.williams@enron.com
4	To: shift.dl-portland@enron.com
5	Subject: Checkouts
6	Mime-Version: 1.0
7	Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii
8	Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
9	X-From: Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=BWILLIA5>
10	X-To: DL-Portland Real Time Shift </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=DL-PortlandRealTimeShift>
11	X-cc: 
12	X-bcc: 
13	X-Folder: \ExMerge - Williams III, Bill\Sent Items
14	X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
15	X-FileName: 
16	
17	Enpower Preschedule Workspace and Path Confirmation
18	
19	Please note we have two new Enpower applications currently in use by the Prescheduling Group that are also available for Real Time use. A manual has been placed in your inbox describing the process in detail. You will be using this in place of Lotus Notes to confirm and process cut power schedules going forward. You must check out with all major marketers and utilities each night. This would include but not be limited to: AEP, AES-New Energy, Aquila, Avista, Calpine, Constellation, Coral, Duke, Dynegy, El Paso Merchant, Exelon, Meico, Mirant, Morgan, NCPA, Reliant, PPLMontana, PowerX, Sempra, SMUD, TransAlta, Williams, and southwest utilities such as Pinnacle West, SRP, PNM, PSCO and Pacificorp. Northwest counterparties are checked out by BPA and do not need to be checked again by us (this would include SCL, TCL, PSPL, BPAP, GCPUD, EWEB, IPC, MPC, SNPD, WWP). These checkouts should be started in HE 19 and finished by HE 21. 
20	
21	NOTE: You must open both PSW and Path Confirmation from your local Enpower Launchpad, which can be found under the Start Menu in Programs/Business Applications/Enpower/Enpower Login. 
22	
23	Following are a few pointers to help you get started. 
24	
25	1.	All prescheduled power paths will be loaded into Path Confirmation. This application must be opened from local Enpower and can be found in the menu that drops down from the hand icon at the left under "Tools."
26	2.	A box will appear asking you to select a default trading desk. Choose "West" and click "Okay."
27	3.	Supply schedules are shown in gray, transmission in yellow, and market in blue.
28	4.	Sort paths by clicking and dragging on the heading you'd like to sort by. Suggestion: Sort by counterparty while making confirmation calls. When all schedules with that counterparty are confirmed, highlight each schedule
29	5.	Highlight the path you'd like to confirm or cut by clicking in the thin box to the very left of the Path Confirmation screen. Highlight multiple rows by holding the "Control" button and while selecting multiple rows.
30	6.	Confirm a path by highlighting and clicking the telephone icon. A screen will come up requesting contact information from the appropriate counterparty. Because this information saves directly to Enpower, save time runs about a minute.
31	7.	Cut a path by highlighting and clicking the scissors icon. A screen called "Cut Information" will come up. Select the "New Path Cut" icon in the upper left-hand corner and supply the relevant information (region, cut time, resupply path, Enpower numbers, Turret ID, etc.)
32	8.	Double click anywhere in a particular row to see a detail of that schedule. This screen will show the terms and hours of the deal as well as volume, price, Enpower deal and OATI tag number.
33	
34	Lotus Notes is being phased out of operation, and we are working with the Enpower team in Houston to develop a discussion database similar to the one we currently use in Notes. These new applications will be a part of that, so please begin adjusting your nightly schedule checkout and/or cuts procedure accordingly (i.e. Record cut paths in Enpower Path Confirmation, not Lotus Notes.)

content.content:
- Nightly schedule checkout calls with counterparties, Portland Real Time desk: Match prescheduled paths against e-tags automatically each night so traders phone only counterparties with a mismatch or cut.. Why: The only evidence is one memo launching the Enpower Path Confirmation tool two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy and the desk's move to UBS. The 2-minute call time is made up. The BPA precedent is a different party doing the calls, not matching. And a later message shows the tag data the matching would depend on leaves Enron's schedules out, which is the kind of error the calls catch. Research that could settle it: Look for messages after December 2001 (UBS Warburg Energy period) showing the nightly checkout still running with many counterparties, how long it takes, and whether tag data is complete enough to confirm schedules without a call.
- Nightly Enpower Path Confirmation checkout with counterparties: Make the Path Confirmation save run in the background and pre-fill each counterparty's contact, so the Real Time trader does not wait about a minute after each of about 27 nightly confirmations.. Why: The only evidence is one launch memo (86.eml, 19 Nov 2001), sent two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy and the desk's move to UBS Warburg on new systems, so nothing shows the 27 nightly Enpower confirmations, or the one-minute save, lasting long enough to save 13.5 hours a month; the full minute counted as lost is also not shown, and another critic already rejected this same nightly checkout work on the same evidence. Research that could settle it: Find messages from December 2001 onward (Enron estate or UBS Warburg Energy) showing the Real Time desk still confirming paths in Enpower Path Confirmation with many counterparties each night, and any complaint or note about the save time, to show the work and the wait continued.

Proposal: Handle Transwestern shippers' short-term contract-quantity changes (one-day or few-day MDQ increases, month-to-month continuations) through a structured request that the marketer approves once and the contract system turns into the amendment, instead of phone, email, forward and hand-drafted amendment

TODAY: A shipper phones the TW marketer (Michelle Lokay), then emails the same terms "per our conversation". The marketer replies or forwards "Approved" to Contract Administration (Dennis Lee or Michael Bodnar), retyping the terms. Contract Admin drafts an amendment and updates the admin contract, then routes it for signature. This happens even for one-day increases.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/2.eml (10 Dec 2001), Julie Reames (BR): "Per our conversation, please increase contract 27748 to 23,115 effective 12/10 for one day only at the $.05 rate plus fuel." Lokay to Dennis Lee: "Approved. / Please increase the Total Quantity from 10000 to 23115 for TODAY.  Points remain the same."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/3.eml (same afternoon, cc Esther Dasilva and Craig Buehler): "Per our earlier conversation, please increase our 27748 MDQ from 10,000 to 16,000 effective 12/11 for one day only." → "Approved."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/4.eml (11 Dec 2001): "please increase contract 27748 to 25,000 for gas day 12th for a rate of $.05." → "Approved. Additional 15,000 on top of the 10,000 that is there all month." The same request was re-forwarded to Michael Bodnar on 13 Dec as "FYI." (corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/15.eml).
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/14.eml (13 Dec 2001): "BRTI and Transwestern agree to increase the MDQ  of transportation contract 27748 from 10,000 MMBtu per day to 33,000 MMBtu per day, effective 12/14/01 - 12/31/01." → "Approved."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/60.eml (31 Dec 2001), TMV: "Please increase the MDQ of TW #27792 by 10000 to 20000/d for January 1-2, 2002 at the same rates." → "Approved.  Amendment to increase TQ by 10,000 for 2 days."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/61.eml (31 Dec 2001), Reliant: "Per our phone conversation, Reliant requests to continue its use of contract  #27496 capacity for the period 1/1-1/31/2002.  Terms of this arrangement will be the same as December's." → "Same as December."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/73.eml (17 Dec 2001), Western Gas: "Approved.  The contract number will remain the same, #27785."
- Amendments pile up and need tracking: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/31.eml: "Amendments # 3 & 4 to Cr 27641 (PPL EnergyPlus) are being routed." and corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/57.eml, PPL: "As for Amendment 3 which increased our West Texas receipts to 14265 during the period described above, I do not see anything.  Can you send me another copy and I will get that signed today."
WHERE IT STALLS: each one-day change goes through three people and two retypings of the same terms (shipper email → marketer "Approved" note → contract admin amendment). BR needed four separate requests for contract 27748 in four days (10-13 Dec).

CHANGE: Put a short-term capacity request form on TW's customer site/EBB (contract, dates, quantity, points, rate). The marketer approves it in the contract system with one click after the phone negotiation. The system generates the amendment from the approved fields, updates the admin contract MDQ for those days, and sends it to the shipper for electronic acceptance. Month-to-month continuations "same as last month" become a one-click roll of the prior amendment.

AFTERWARDS: No forwarding or retyping. Contract Admin handles only non-standard amendments, such as the PPL Red Rock receipt-point restructurings in 164.eml.

ESTIMATE: Per short-term request today: marketer reads and forwards with retyped terms, about 3 min; Contract Admin drafts and updates the amendment and admin contract, about 15 min; follow-up or re-forwards, about 2 min. That is about 20 min, versus about 4 min afterwards (marketer approval plus an admin glance), so about 16 min saved. Frequency: Lokay's mailbox alone shows 7 such requests from 10 Dec to 31 Dec 2001 (2, 3, 4, 14, 60, 61, 73). I conservatively use 6 a month for her accounts alone. 6 × 16 = 96 min ≈ 1.6 h/month × $85 ≈ $136/month. Other TW marketers' accounts (Lindberg, Lohman, Y'Barbo, McConnell) likely add similar volume but are not counted.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The idea might be workable, but the evidence doesn't support the savings, and the same work and change were already rejected in `decisions.md`.

**What's wrong:**

1. **The work may not have continued long enough to save anything.** The only source is one memo, `corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/86.eml` (19 Nov 2001). It introduces Path Confirmation as a new tool, two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy. Later memos to the same shift show the business shrinking:
   - 30 Nov (`62.eml`): "EPE ... are no longer selling to us", "We will be zeroing Enpower deals out on Monday", and "As of Jan 01, 2002 we will no longer be marketing for EPE".
   - 4 Dec (`61.eml`): the desk is busy with "more and more cuts".

   Nothing shows 25 counterparties with schedules being confirmed every night of the month.
2. **Half the savings is made up.** The mail never mentions the "about 1 minute" of typing contact details, or retyping the same details every night. The pop-up asks for "contact information from the appropriate counterparty", which may well be whoever answered the call that night, so pre-filling might save little. The claim that the work "competes with live real-time trading" is also not in the mail.
3. **The one-minute wait may not all be lost.** The memo does state that the save takes "about a minute". But it doesn't show whether the trader sits idle during it or dials the next counterparty. It also doesn't show whether there is one save per counterparty or one per path.
4. **It duplicates earlier rejections.** `decisions.md` already rejects "Nightly Enpower Path Confirmation checkout with counterparties", the same background save and pre-filled contacts. It also rejects a related nightly-checkout proposal, both on this same memo.

**Research that could change the verdict:** messages from December 2001 onward (Enron estate or UBS Warburg Energy) showing the Real Time desk still confirming many counterparties' paths in Path Confirmation each night. Any note about the save time or about entering contact details would help too.

Rejection file: `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2\proposals\reject-path-confirmation-prefill.json`

content.text:
I rejected this proposal. The idea might work, but the evidence for how often this happens doesn't hold up. The rejection is recorded in `decisions.md`.

**What checks out:** Every quote matches the mail. The process is as described: the shipper phones, then emails "per our conversation", Lokay forwards "Approved" to Dennis Lee or Michael Bodnar, and Contract Admin writes an amendment. 60.eml says "Amendment to increase TQ by 10,000 for 2 days."

**What is wrong:**
1. **The rate is a one-month burst.** All six separate requests (2, 3, 4, 14, 60/61, 73) are dated 10–31 Dec 2001. 15.eml and 59.eml are just re-forwards of 4 and 60. Lokay's sent mail runs from late Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and is busy from January to March (about 100 messages). I searched it for "one day", "MDQ", "per our conversation", "same as December/January" and "increase…contract/TQ" and found no short-term requests after December. The only nearby amendment is PPL's (57.eml, 164.eml), and that is a multi-month change to receipt points, which the proposal itself leaves to Contract Admin. Six requests over roughly four months is about 1.5 a month, not 6. December 2001 was also the month right after Enron's bankruptcy filing, so it may not be a normal month.
2. **The minutes are partly invented and overstated.**
   - **Retyping:** The "two retypings" claim is wrong for several cases. In 3.eml and 14.eml Lokay forwards a bare "Approved." and retypes nothing.
   - **Contract Admin time:** The 15 minutes per amendment has nothing in the mail behind it.
   - **The re-forward to Bodnar:** 15.eml is more likely a handover to a new contact than a sign that the process stalls.
3. **Cost against benefit.** At about 1.5 a month and 16 minutes each, the saving is roughly 25 minutes a month (about $35). That is far too little to pay for a request form on the customer website, a link to the contract system and electronic acceptance of amendments.

**Research that could change the verdict:**
- Short-term MDQ increases or month-to-month continuations outside December 2001, in the mail of Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar or the other TW marketers (Lindberg, Lohman, Y'Barbo, McConnell).
- Any sign of how long Contract Admin spends on a one-day amendment, such as status lists like Buehler's "Contract Status" emails (inbox/72.eml) that count these amendments.

summary:
I rejected this proposal. The idea might work, but the evidence for how often this happens doesn't hold up. The rejection is recorded in `decisions.md`.

**What checks out:** Every quote matches the mail. The process is as described: the shipper phones, then emails "per our conversation", Lokay forwards "Approved" to Dennis Lee or Michael Bodnar, and Contract Admin writes an amendment. 60.eml says "Amendment to increase TQ by 10,000 for 2 days."

**What is wrong:**
1. **The rate is a one-month burst.** All six separate requests (2, 3, 4, 14, 60/61, 73) are dated 10–31 Dec 2001. 15.eml and 59.eml are just re-forwards of 4 and 60. Lokay's sent mail runs from late Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and is busy from January to March (about 100 messages). I searched it for "one day", "MDQ", "per our conversation", "same as December/January" and "increase…contract/TQ" and found no short-term requests after December. The only nearby amendment is PPL's (57.eml, 164.eml), and that is a multi-month change to receipt points, which the proposal itself leaves to Contract Admin. Six requests over roughly four months is about 1.5 a month, not 6. December 2001 was also the month right after Enron's bankruptcy filing, so it may not be a normal month.
2. **The minutes are partly invented and overstated.**
   - **Retyping:** The "two retypings" claim is wrong for several cases. In 3.eml and 14.eml Lokay forwards a bare "Approved." and retypes nothing.
   - **Contract Admin time:** The 15 minutes per amendment has nothing in the mail behind it.
   - **The re-forward to Bodnar:** 15.eml is more likely a handover to a new contact than a sign that the process stalls.
3. **Cost against benefit.** At about 1.5 a month and 16 minutes each, the saving is roughly 25 minutes a month (about $35). That is far too little to pay for a request form on the customer website, a link to the contract system and electronic acceptance of amendments.

**Research that could change the verdict:**
- Short-term MDQ increases or month-to-month continuations outside December 2001, in the mail of Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar or the other TW marketers (Lindberg, Lohman, Y'Barbo, McConnell).
- Any sign of how long Contract Admin spends on a one-day amendment, such as status lists like Buehler's "Contract Status" emails (inbox/72.eml) that count these amendments.

Rejection file: `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2\proposals\tw-short-term-mdq-requests-reject.json`

content.content:
68	- Researching HPLC-ENA intercompany accrual variances: Have Sitara create the mirror side of every HPLC-ENA intercompany deal automatically, and add a daily intercompany nomination tie-out. Why: The mail shows an intercompany deal is already one shared Sitara deal (868: 'Intercompany Sitara deals are the same'); the missing sides are unmatched nominations and accruals, not missing deal tickets, so auto-creating mirror tickets would not remove them, and the claim that monthly recurrence is shown rests on one month's list. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how the ENA side of an intercompany Sitara deal gets nominated and why it goes missing (the 'system limitation' Lenart asks about in 868), plus intercompany variance lists for other months, to support a proposal built only on a daily nomination tie-out.
69	- Daily forwarding of the Energy Market Report to West traders: Have the report go straight to a West-traders distribution list, so nobody forwards it by hand.. Why: The same work and change is already saved as decision 17 ("Daily forward of the Energy Market Report to West Power traders"), which cites all seven of these messages, so saving it again would count the same saving twice.
70	- Monthly roll-forward of Texas desk transport usage tickets in Sitara: Have Sitara roll transport usage tickets into each new month by itself, with rates taken from the rate table used for invoicing, so accounting only reviews a list of gaps.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 11 in decisions.md (Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets), citing the same messages.
71	- Monthly roll of Texas transport usage tickets: Let Sitara transport usage tickets run for the whole contract term, take their rates from the rate matrix automatically, and carry last month's volumes forward.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets', which cites the same messages (1144, 1145, 1257, 1796, 2109, 2111, 867).
72	- Monthly repricing of EnerVest Sitara deal S#27239: Let the monthly EnerVest price be set without an email to the risk desk: either model the deal's real pricing in Sitara, or let settlements enter it with the desk reviewing afterwards.. Why: This work is already saved in decisions.md as item 17, 'Monthly repricing of invoice-priced Sitara deals (27239 EnerVest, 27253)', which cites the same six messages and proposes the same change.
73	- Monthly EWS admin-assistant roster check: Build the monthly admin-assistant list from HR/directory data and ask assistants to reply only when their record changed or is blank.. Why: The same work and change are already saved in decisions.md as item 8, 'Monthly EWS admin-assistant roster check' ($134.30 a month), which cites the same single message, williams-w3/sent_items/313.eml, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
74	- Daily hand-forwarding of the Energy Market Report to West power traders: Send the vendor's daily report straight to a distribution list of the 12 traders, or forward it with an automatic mail rule, so nobody forwards it by hand.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 19 in decisions.md, 'Daily forward of the Energy Market Report to West Power traders' ($8.50 a month), which cites all seven of these messages, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
75	- Monthly P&L support for Arthur Andersen gas testing: Save each gas book's month-end P&L top page, five largest-day top pages and curve-shift reports to a dated folder AA can read, so nobody pulls them on request.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 5 in decisions.md, 'Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen', which cites the same eight messages, so saving this would count the saving twice.
76	- Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration Report: Have the contract system produce the report on a fixed date before each bid week and email it to a list people join or leave themselves, so Cheryl only checks it.. Why: The same work is already saved in decisions.md as item 13, with the same change and the same messages (farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, 2114.eml), so saving it again would count it twice.
77	- ENA/Burlington capacity-release 50/50 marketing-fee split on TW billing: Configure TW billing to compute ENA's release credit and TW's marketing fee for contract 24924 automatically each month. Why: The mail shows a single one-off deal on one contract, seen for two months (a release effective 1/11/02 - 1/31/02 and then February), with no sign it continues; building custom billing logic for it would cost more than the roughly $71 a month it saves, and the part that actually stalls (whether TW pays ENA its half while ENA owes TW money) is a judgment call that billing logic cannot settle. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing that this release, or other releases with fee-sharing terms, ran for many more months or across several shippers, and for anything saying how CBS handles such terms; if neither exists, the verdict stands.
78	- Monthly Investor Relations volumetric explanations: Have the Statistical Database flag the +/-10% variances, show EOL and counterparty drivers, pre-fill last month's explanation, and collect the controllers' explanations in the database instead of by email.. Why: The change depends on things the mail does not show: that the Statistical Database holds EOL and counterparty detail, and that it does not already show the variances. The minutes are also inflated: 11 controllers' work is costed from one controller's two-line reply, and 11 readings are counted for a verifier who was copied only because one controller chose to copy him. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what the Statistical Database contains (variance columns, EOL or counterparty breakdowns), replies from controllers other than Baumbach, and other months' requests, and use them to show how long the explanations take and whether they repeat; then cost only the steps the change really removes.
79	- Monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations: Pre-fill each region's previous explanation next to every +/-10% variance in the Statistical Database, so controllers tick 'same driver' or type a new one there instead of replying by email.. Why: The same work was already rejected in decisions.md for the same gaps, and this version repeats them: 11 controllers' time is costed from one controller's (Baumbach's) one- and three-line replies, 'answers repeat' rests on one region in two months, and the change drops the stated rule that 'the volumes be verified by commercial personnel' for repeated drivers. Research that could settle it: Find replies from controllers other than Baumbach and requests for other months, showing how long the explanations take and whether drivers really repeat across regions; then cost only the steps the change removes (email reply and BA&R consolidation) and keep the commercial verification of volumes every month.

Proposal: Make the month-end basis/index roll-off a system setting in the gas risk calc, producing the TDS (100% prompt basis) and V@R/Benchmark (50/50 roll) views from one calc, instead of each book administrator calculating, officializing, unofficializing and recalculating every book by hand

TODAY: At each monthly roll-off (prompt-month expiry), the gas risk lead (Jeff Gossett) emails the book administrators instructions. Each admin calcs every basis book twice for each roll-off night, once with 100% basis for the TDS download and once with 50% basis rolled off for V@R, toggling officialization in between. Index positions are rolled off and rolled in by hand 50% each night over two nights.

Hi Dutch,

I was hoping you could spread the word to the book admins regarding a data 
entry methodology requirement for Gas Daily 4 legged deals. The Confirms 
group is working with Ricky Dang to expand the logic and capabilities of 
their systems to accomodate automated confirms on deals done in the new 
format, but in order for this to work, it is critical that all Gas Daily 4 
legged deals entered manually into TAGG be booked in the same leg order as 
those which bridge automatically. Although the legs can technically be 
entered in any order as far as Risk is concerned, such deviations will cause 
failures from the confirm end. If the Gas Daily book admins can follow the 
same entry order used in deal # Q25289.1, .2, .3, .4 , the Confirms Group 
should be able to work with it from there. Just let me know if this will 
create any problems from your end. Thanks!

Torrey

-----Original Message-----
From: 	Symes, Kate  
Sent:	Tuesday, August 14, 2001 11:13 AM
To:	Williams III, Bill
Subject:	A few reminders....

Bill - does this sound reasonable? Do you have anything to add?


Please make a note of the following. I know we have several new traders, and details often get overlooked in the midst of the learning process. But this is not only information for the new guys a reminder for the old that attention to detail is an important part of the job. Thanks.

1. Purchases made under one book must be sold under the same book. Pay attention when extending deals. If you don't purchase the energy in a particular book, you don't have energy to sell from that book.

2. Specify EPEC as the group when entering deals for El Paso. Also, pay attention to detail with EPE spinning reserves (as a violation is extremely expensive for EPE), also curtail units in the right order. Copper then Newman 4 then Four Corners (Be sure to curtail Four Corners before selling under cost!)

3. El Paso model must tie out with CARP when trading day is done. Check spreadsheet formulas. 

4. El Paso totals should be logged in the reconciliation model (m://electric/epe/epe01/aug01/epe reconciliation model) and all variances explained.

5. Bloomberg deals need to be assigned a $15 FLAT broker fee per trade. If you begin a deal with Bloomberg trades, enter a per-megawatt fee, and extend the deal later with bilateral trades, you're effectively charging yourself extra brokerage because THAT FEE WILL BE ASSIGNED TO EVERY MW IN YOUR DEAL. Can someone come up with a compelling reason why we wouldn't simply multiply $15 times the number of Bloomberg trades done? huh?Please let me know.

6. Most importantly, if you are unsure, call someone who is not.

Thanks again for your attention to these matters.

Kate

57	Subject: requests for new curves, new books, porfolio changes
58	
59	In the past few months, the procedures for setting up new curves and books 
60	have not been followed by everyone. 
61	
62	The following memo documents the procedures to 1) set up a new curve, 2) set 
63	up a new book, and 3) change a portfolio hierarchy.  Please note that risk 
64	management (for each commodity group), "risk management"  is responsible for 
65	ensuring that information is flowing appropriately between the valuation 
66	systems and RisktRAC (Risk Analysis and Reporting can help, but do not have 
67	all of the ERMS information to be able to ensure the completeness of 
68	RisktRAC).
69	
70	I have attached the request form for each of these changes at the bottom of 
71	this memo.  Please ensure that everyone in your group obtains a copy. 
72	
73	The procedure to set up a new curve is as follows:
74	
75	Trader starts trading at a new location or a new commodity and needs a new 
76	curve set up
77	Trader communicates this to risk management
78	Risk management constructs new curve in ERMS (with the help of the IT 
79	department)
80	Risk management completes a curve set up request form to set up curve in 
81	RisktRAC
82	Curve form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
83	Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up curve in RisktRAC
84	A system generated message is sent to people on the "curve list" indicating a 
85	change in the RisktRAC curves has been made
86	
87	If the curve is not set up in RisktRAC the positions are not captured in the 
88	VAR or engine, thereby making VAR inaccurate.  As a side note, Risk Analysis 
89	and Reporting has implemented a new process in which on a weekly basis new 
90	curves set up in ERMS are reviewed to ensure that these have been set up in 
91	RisktRAC.  We did this for the first time today and noted numerous curves in 
92	ERMS that are not in RisktRAC - which we are working with you to resolve.
93	
94	The procedure to set up a new book in RisktRAC is as follows:
95	
96	Trader/risk management determines new book is needed
97	New book request form (for RisktRAC) is completed by risk management
98	New book request form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
99	Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up book in RisktRAC
100	Risk Analysis and Reporting forwards request to ERMS administrator and global 
101	counterparty group to request that book is set up in valuation and 
102	counterparty systems
103	Once all groups have completed their individual set ups, a final e-mail is 
104	sent to personnel on the "books list" and the book administrator in the risk 
105	management department who requested the book
106

Burton McIntyre/HOU/ECT@ECT 
Subject: requests for new curves, new books, porfolio changes

In the past few months, the procedures for setting up new curves and books 
have not been followed by everyone. 

The following memo documents the procedures to 1) set up a new curve, 2) set 
up a new book, and 3) change a portfolio hierarchy.  Please note that risk 
management (for each commodity group), "risk management"  is responsible for 
ensuring that information is flowing appropriately between the valuation 
systems and RisktRAC (Risk Analysis and Reporting can help, but do not have 
all of the ERMS information to be able to ensure the completeness of 
RisktRAC).

I have attached the request form for each of these changes at the bottom of 
this memo.  Please ensure that everyone in your group obtains a copy. 

The procedure to set up a new curve is as follows:

Trader starts trading at a new location or a new commodity and needs a new 
curve set up
Trader communicates this to risk management
Risk management constructs new curve in ERMS (with the help of the IT 
department)
Risk management completes a curve set up request form to set up curve in 
RisktRAC
Curve form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up curve in RisktRAC
A system generated message is sent to people on the "curve list" indicating a 
change in the RisktRAC curves has been made

If the curve is not set up in RisktRAC the positions are not captured in the 
VAR or engine, thereby making VAR inaccurate.  As a side note, Risk Analysis 
and Reporting has implemented a new process in which on a weekly basis new 
curves set up in ERMS are reviewed to ensure that these have been set up in 
RisktRAC.  We did this for the first time today and noted numerous curves in 
ERMS that are not in RisktRAC - which we are working with you to resolve.

The procedure to set up a new book in RisktRAC is as follows:

Trader/risk management determines new book is needed
New book request form (for RisktRAC) is completed by risk management
New book request form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up book in RisktRAC
Risk Analysis and Reporting forwards request to ERMS administrator and global 
counterparty group to request that book is set up in valuation and 
counterparty systems
Once all groups have completed their individual set ups, a final e-mail is 
sent to personnel on the "books list" and the book administrator in the risk 
management department who requested the book

It is important that there is a one to one link between the ERMS and RisktRAC 
books, or not all positions will be captured in RisktRAC (two commodities per 
ERMS book does not flow properly into RisktRAC).

The above two processes have formally existed for a number of months.  
Additionally, we are formalizing the procedure for changing portfolio 
hierarchies.  The procedure now is:

Risk management is responsible for requesting all portfolio hierarchy 
changes.  Previously, changes could be made through a request by Risk 
Analysis and Reporting or RAC.  These two groups are no longer allowed to 
submit change requests.  All requests must come through risk management.
Risk management completes a request, including the reason for the requested 
change in structure
Risk management forwards the request to Risk Analysis and Reporting
Risk Analysis and Reporting makes the change and notifies risk management 
that the change has been made.

If you have any questions, comments or concerns, please call: me X39123, 
Chris Abel X33012, Burton McIntyre X57197, or Susan Trevino X31462.

Thanks,

Shona
