Why: The only evidence is one launch memo (86.eml, 19 Nov 2001), sent two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy and the desk's move to UBS Warburg on new systems, so nothing shows the 27 nightly Enpower confirmations, or the one-minute save, lasting long enough to save 13.5 hours a month; the full minute counted as lost is also not shown, and another critic already rejected this same nightly checkout work on the same evidence. Research that could settle it: Find messages from December 2001 onward (Enron estate or UBS Warburg Energy) showing the Real Time desk still confirming paths in Enpower Path Confirmation with many counterparties each night, and any complaint or note about the save time, to show the work and the wait continued.
61	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale as a standing zero-price ticket and price the HPL-to-ENA demand tickets by formula (firm volume x the month's index), so only the crude value is keyed monthly.. Why: The same change to the same work is already saved in decisions.md (item 7). This version also gets today's process wrong: the mail shows the monthly steps were not done at all from March 2001 on and had to be caught up months later, not keyed by hand each month before flash.
62	- Redirecting mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams: Have IT add department and location to both Bill Williams directory names so senders can tell them apart when addressing.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Correcting mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams' (item 8 in decisions.md), which uses 9 of this proposal's 16 occurrences, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
63	- Monthly auditor requests for gas P&L top pages and curve shift reports: At month-end, copy every book's daily P&L top pages and curve shift reports into one read-only audit folder that the auditors pull from themselves.. Why: This is already saved as item 4 in decisions.md ('Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen'), which cites the same eight messages and makes the same change, so saving it again would count the savings twice.
64	- Supplying P&L top pages and curve shift reports for Arthur Andersen's monthly gas testing: Each month-end, file the official P&L top pages and curve shift reports for every gas book in a read-only folder that AA can open, so AA stops asking the desks for them.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as item 4 in decisions.md, 'Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen', which cites all of this proposal's messages (201, 299, 326, 327, 420, 515, 516, 583), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
65	- Monthly repricing of EnerVest deal S#27239: Let Settlements set the invoiced price on deal S#27239 when it processes the EnerVest invoice, instead of emailing Risk to do it each month.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 14 in decisions.md, 'Monthly repricing of invoice-priced Sitara deals (27239 EnerVest, 27253)', which cites all six of these messages and proposes the same change.
66	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas/crude swap deal tickets: Book the GLO sale at zero price permanently and make the HPL-ENA and ENA-EGM demand tickets evergreen with formula amounts, so the only monthly input is the crude value.. Why: decisions.md already has the same work and the same change saved (item 9, $55.25 a month), and the mail shows the swap ran only from January to May 2001, so it was a short episode, not ongoing monthly work.
67	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude intercompany tickets: Set up the GLO/EGM intercompany legs as standing deals whose demand charges are calculated each month, with a check before flash, instead of zeroing prices and keying tickets by hand.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 10 in decisions.md, 'Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets' ($55.25 a month), which cites the same messages (175.eml, 83.eml, 28.eml), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
68	- Researching HPLC-ENA intercompany accrual variances: Have Sitara create the mirror side of every HPLC-ENA intercompany deal automatically, and add a daily intercompany nomination tie-out. Why: The mail shows an intercompany deal is already one shared Sitara deal (868: 'Intercompany Sitara deals are the same'); the missing sides are unmatched nominations and accruals, not missing deal tickets, so auto-creating mirror tickets would not remove them, and the claim that monthly recurrence is shown rests on one month's list. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how the ENA side of an intercompany Sitara deal gets nominated and why it goes missing (the 'system limitation' Lenart asks about in 868), plus intercompany variance lists for other months, to support a proposal built only on a daily nomination tie-out.
69	- Daily forwarding of the Energy Market Report to West traders: Have the report go straight to a West-traders distribution list, so nobody forwards it by hand.. Why: The same work and change is already saved as decision 17 ("Daily forward of the Energy Market Report to West Power traders"), which cites all seven of these messages, so saving it again would count the same saving twice.
70	- Monthly roll-forward of Texas desk transport usage tickets in Sitara: Have Sitara roll transport usage tickets into each new month by itself, with rates taken from the rate table used for invoicing, so accounting only reviews a list of gaps.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 11 in decisions.md (Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets), citing the same messages.
71	- Monthly roll of Texas transport usage tickets: Let Sitara transport usage tickets run for the whole contract term, take their rates from the rate matrix automatically, and carry last month's volumes forward.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets', which cites the same messages (1144, 1145, 1257, 1796, 2109, 2111, 867).
72	- Monthly repricing of EnerVest Sitara deal S#27239: Let the monthly EnerVest price be set without an email to the risk desk: either model the deal's real pricing in Sitara, or let settlements enter it with the desk reviewing afterwards.. Why: This work is already saved in decisions.md as item 17, 'Monthly repricing of invoice-priced Sitara deals (27239 EnerVest, 27253)', which cites the same six messages and proposes the same change.
73	- Monthly EWS admin-assistant roster check: Build the monthly admin-assistant list from HR/directory data and ask assistants to reply only when their record changed or is blank.. Why: The same work and change are already saved in decisions.md as item 8, 'Monthly EWS admin-assistant roster check' ($134.30 a month), which cites the same single message, williams-w3/sent_items/313.eml, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
74	- Daily hand-forwarding of the Energy Market Report to West power traders: Send the vendor's daily report straight to a distribution list of the 12 traders, or forward it with an automatic mail rule, so nobody forwards it by hand.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 19 in decisions.md, 'Daily forward of the Energy Market Report to West Power traders' ($8.50 a month), which cites all seven of these messages, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
75	- Monthly P&L support for Arthur Andersen gas testing: Save each gas book's month-end P&L top page, five largest-day top pages and curve-shift reports to a dated folder AA can read, so nobody pulls them on request.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 5 in decisions.md, 'Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen', which cites the same eight messages, so saving this would count the saving twice.
76	- Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration Report: Have the contract system produce the report on a fixed date before each bid week and email it to a list people join or leave themselves, so Cheryl only checks it.. Why: The same work is already saved in decisions.md as item 13, with the same change and the same messages (farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, 2114.eml), so saving it again would count it twice.
77	- ENA/Burlington capacity-release 50/50 marketing-fee split on TW billing: Configure TW billing to compute ENA's release credit and TW's marketing fee for contract 24924 automatically each month. Why: The mail shows a single one-off deal on one contract, seen for two months (a release effective 1/11/02 - 1/31/02 and then February), with no sign it continues; building custom billing logic for it would cost more than the roughly $71 a month it saves, and the part that actually stalls (whether TW pays ENA its half while ENA owes TW money) is a judgment call that billing logic cannot settle. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing that this release, or other releases with fee-sharing terms, ran for many more months or across several shippers, and for anything saying how CBS handles such terms; if neither exists, the verdict stands.
78	- Monthly Investor Relations volumetric explanations: Have the Statistical Database flag the +/-10% variances, show EOL and counterparty drivers, pre-fill last month's explanation, and collect the controllers' explanations in the database instead of by email.. Why: The change depends on things the mail does not show: that the Statistical Database holds EOL and counterparty detail, and that it does not already show the variances. The minutes are also inflated: 11 controllers' work is costed from one controller's two-line reply, and 11 readings are counted for a verifier who was copied only because one controller chose to copy him. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what the Statistical Database contains (variance columns, EOL or counterparty breakdowns), replies from controllers other than Baumbach, and other months' requests, and use them to show how long the explanations take and whether they repeat; then cost only the steps the change really removes.
79	- Monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations: Pre-fill each region's previous explanation next to every +/-10% variance in the Statistical Database, so controllers tick 'same driver' or type a new one there instead of replying by email.. Why: The same work was already rejected in decisions.md for the same gaps, and this version repeats them: 11 controllers' time is costed from one controller's (Baumbach's) one- and three-line replies, 'answers repeat' rests on one region in two months, and the change drops the stated rule that 'the volumes be verified by commercial personnel' for repeated drivers. Research that could settle it: Find replies from controllers other than Baumbach and requests for other months, showing how long the explanations take and whether drivers really repeat across regions; then cost only the steps the change removes (email reply and BA&R consolidation) and keep the commercial verification of volumes every month.
80	- Monthly gas curve-validation questions: Send each month's curve-validation questions straight to the owning trader from a maintained curve-owner list, and validate derived curves such as NGI-PGE/TOPOCK through their parent curve.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as item 15 in decisions.md ('Monthly gas curve validation questions', $28.05 a month), citing the same messages 132, 170, 47 and 49. This version also gets the facts wrong: only the January round went through Gossett and three leads. February and March went straight to the leads and then to Giron alone. TOPOCK was flagged only once. And the March re-ask came back unchanged even after Giron asked the trader directly.
81	- Nightly counterparty checkouts in Enpower Path Confirmation, Portland Real Time desk: Pre-fill counterparty contact details and make the Path Confirmation save run in the background, one batch per counterparty.. Why: The only evidence is one memo launching the tool (86.eml, 19 Nov 2001), sent two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy while counterparties were already stopping trades with Enron; nothing shows 25 counterparties being confirmed every night for long, the one minute of contact typing and the retyping of the same contacts are made up, and this same work and change were already rejected in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find messages from December 2001 onward (Enron estate or UBS Warburg Energy) showing the Real Time desk still confirming many counterparties' paths in Enpower Path Confirmation each night, with any note on save time or contact entry.
82	- Settling Real Time CAISO congestion-relief revenue: Take congestion revenue straight from CAPS finals into the daily flash, with an automatic exception list against the inc sheet, instead of trader emails, hand calculations and month-end true-up chases. Why: Most of the claimed saving rests on misreadings: the largest item (the desk's daily exposure tally, 150 of 370 minutes) is a net-position check the manager asked for and the change would not replace; Jim's hand calculation in 90.eml was a stopgap while the system was down ('When the system comes up'), and he says Volume Management 'haven't missed it for a long time'; the mail shows about 2 events a month, not 4; and once these are corrected, the added daily review of the exception list cancels most of what remains. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that congestion revenue is routinely left out of the flash month after month (true-ups like 266.eml beyond August 2001), and for how long Volume Management actually spends on each event when the system is up, to see whether a narrower check of the flash against CAPS saves real time.
83	- Transwestern short-term contract-quantity changes: Shippers submit one-day or few-day MDQ increases and month-to-month continuations on a web form; the marketer approves with one click and the contract system generates the amendment.. Why: The rate is not supported: all six distinct requests fall in 10-31 Dec 2001, and Lokay's sent mail from January to late March 2002 (about 100 messages) has none, so 6 a month is a one-month burst projected forward. The 15-minute amendment step is also assumed, and the marketer mostly forwards a one-word 'Approved.' rather than retyping terms. Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ or continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, Lindberg, Lohman, Y'Barbo, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Admin spends on a one-day amendment.
84	- Second, unposted TW Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the TW team once whether anyone uses Rita Bianchi's second Current Shipper rate matrix and stop keeping it up if nobody does.. Why: The work shows up only once in the archive (29 Oct 2001), and nothing says how often the Current Shipper rates change, so the quarterly or monthly rate behind the saving is a guess. Research that could settle it: Look for other TW rate-matrix postings or Current Shipper rate changes, such as earlier MATRIX*.doc files, Global Settlement surcharge updates, or Rita Bianchi's or Elizabeth Brown's mail, that show how often the rates change; and for any reply saying whether anyone uses the spreadsheet.
85	- Transwestern shippers' short-term contract change requests: Shippers send MDQ increases and month-to-month continuations through a structured request; the account director approves with one click and the system produces the amendment for contract admin to check.. Why: The rate of 8-9 a month comes from a three-week burst (10 Dec 2001 - 3 Jan 2002): Lokay's sent mail runs from 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and holds only about 10 such requests in all, about 2 a month, so at the proposal's own 15 minutes the saving is roughly 30 minutes a month, too little to pay for a shipper web form; the 15-minute amendment step is also assumed, and the same work was already rejected for this reason (decisions.md Rejected item 83). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, extension or continuation requests in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell) outside December 2001, and anything showing how long Contract Admin spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
86	- Weekly purchase-requisition processing by Mary Poorman: Move requisitions to SAP purchasing self-service with automatic approval routing and a named backup, so the coordinator handles only exceptions.. Why: The only evidence is one offhand remark in a message of doubtful origin (482.eml) that says nothing about the steps, volume or tools of the requisition work, so neither the SAP self-service fix nor the 10-hours-a-week saving can be shown from the mail. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows the requisition work happening: requisitions sent to or by Poorman, approval chases, purchasing or SAP requisition system mail, counts per week, and where the time goes. Confirm the message's origin against normal mail as well.
87	- Next-day long/short position notices to the Real Time shift: Replace typed 'Short/Long/Length for <day>' emails with an automatic next-day open-position view from Enpower that the shift checks at shift start. Why: The mail shows Real Time can already read these positions in Enpower (120.eml, 'according to Enpower, STNW is long on peak @ PGE System'), and the emails exist to carry what Enpower does not hold: deals booked only in CAPS (512.eml, 112.eml 'built in Caps but not in enpower', with Bill telling them to hold the Enpower deal until the next day), which deal number to link, and where to deliver or sell (120.eml, 172.eml), so the proposed view would not remove the notices. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that the notices mostly repeat data already correct in Enpower and carry no delivery or CAPS-only information; if so, a narrower change, such as a required template or a check against Enpower before sending (Kate's suggestion in 120.eml), might be proposed instead.
88	- Transwestern shippers' short-term capacity changes: Shippers submit one- or two-day MDQ increases, extensions and month-to-month continuations as a standard electronic request; the marketer click-approves and the system generates the amendment and updates the admin contract.. Why: The rate of about 8 a month comes from a three-week burst (10-31 Dec 2001) plus two long-term Red Rock receipt amendments (164.eml, 57.eml) that are not short-term changes; Lokay's sent mail runs 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and shows no short-term request after 3 Jan 2002, so the real rate is about 1-2 a month, and the same work has already been rejected twice for this reason (decisions.md Rejected items 83 and 85). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, one-day extension or monthly continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Administration spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
89

content.text:
I saved the proposal. It is item 3 of 22 in `decisions.md`, at 330 minutes a month, which comes to 5.5 hours or $467.50 a month.

**What the mail supports:**
- **The work:** In `corpus/giron-d/sent/631.eml` (27 Sep 2000), Gossett sends the steps to five book administrators. He then forwards them to six West administrators, Giron among them, and Giron passes them on to Kevin Radous. The steps are to calc twice ("calc your 100% basis calc first. Officialize. Load your positions into TDS. Unofficialize. Calc your 50% basis calc. Officialize."). Basis rolls off 50% each night, and index rolls 50% "tonight" and 50% "tommorrow".
- **How often:** "Again this month" shows it happens every month, and the November roll-off in `corpus/giron-d/sent/442.eml` shows it continues.
- **Where it stalls:** In 442.eml, four traders' basis was not rolled off on the Benchmark. Gossett asks how to stop that happening, and Giron replies "My fault on Tomas, I didn't remind Kevin."
- **The estimate:** 11 administrators each spend about 15 minutes a night on the extra calc over two nights. That is realistic, possibly low, for a second calc, two officialization steps and a separate post ID. The saving counts Gossett's instruction email and follow-up and takes off the time someone would spend reviewing the new exception list.

**What I changed before saving:**
- **Index roll-off:** The original said index positions are rolled "by hand". The mail only says "we will roll-off 50%", so I took out the claim that it is done manually.
- **Rate:** I set the stated rate to once a month, citing "Again this month".
- **Wording:** I tightened the text into plain words.

**Not a duplicate:** Saved item 7, the nightly check that every book is marked official, is about something different, which is forgetting to officialize at all. No saved or rejected proposal covers the monthly roll-off.

The proposal is at `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2\proposals\basis-index-rolloff-setting.json`.

Load your positions into TDS. Unofficialize. Calc your 50% basis calc. Officialize."). Basis rolls off 50% each night, and index rolls 50% "tonight" and 50% "tommorrow".

- **Where it stalls:** In 442.eml, four traders' basis was not rolled off on the Benchmark. Gossett asks how to stop that happening, and Giron replies "My fault on Tomas, I didn't remind Kevin."
- **The estimate:** 11 administrators each spend about 15 minutes a night on the extra calc over two nights. That is realistic, possibly low, for a second calc, two officialization steps and a separate post ID. The saving counts Gossett's instruction email and follow-up and takes off the time someone would spend reviewing the new exception list.

**What I changed before saving:**
- **Index roll-off:** The original said index positions are rolled "by hand". The mail only says "we will roll-off 50%", so I took out the claim that it is done manually.
- **Rate:** I set the stated rate to once a month, citing "Again this month".
- **Wording:** I tightened the text into plain words.

**Not a duplicate:** Saved item 7, the nightly check that every book is marked official, is about something different, which is forgetting to officialize at all. No saved or rejected proposal covers the monthly roll-off.

Proposal: When a risk manager creates a new forward curve in ERMS, set it up automatically in RisktRAC (V@R) and TAGG and flag gaps nightly, replacing the paper request forms, the separate TAGG email request, and Risk Analysis & Reporting's weekly manual ERMS-vs-RisktRAC curve review

TODAY: A new curve is built in ERMS by the desk's risk manager. It then needs (a) a "curve set up request form" sent to Risk Analysis and Reporting (RAR), who key it into RisktRAC, and (b) a separate email to the TAGG administrator (Jeremy Wong) to add it to TAGG. Because steps get skipped, RAR now compares ERMS against RisktRAC by hand every week.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/410.eml (Shona Wilson memo, 22 Nov 2000, to about 30 risk leads; forwarded by Susan Trevino to Giron and by Giron to Anne Bike): "In the past few months, the procedures for setting up new curves and books have not been followed by everyone." / "Risk management constructs new curve in ERMS (with the help of the IT department) / Risk management completes a curve set up request form to set up curve in RisktRAC / Curve form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting / Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up curve in RisktRAC" / "If the curve is not set up in RisktRAC the positions are not captured in the VAR or engine, thereby making VAR inaccurate." / "Risk Analysis and Reporting has implemented a new process in which on a weekly basis new curves set up in ERMS are reviewed to ensure that these have been set up in RisktRAC.  We did this for the first time today and noted numerous curves in ERMS that are not in RisktRAC - which we are working with you to resolve."
- The separate TAGG request: corpus/giron-d/sent/573.eml (19 Oct 2000), Giron to Jeremy Wong: "I have added two curves in Publ Names:  WY/WELLHEAD and WY/MKTZONE.  They are in curveview.  Please add them to Tagg." with Wong's reply in corpus/giron-d/sent/569.eml: "Done." Also corpus/giron-d/sent/411.eml (7 Dec 2000): "I set up these new curves this morning and need them added to Tagg / NGI-MOJAVE / GDP-MOJAVE / GDP-PGE/TOPOCK".
WHERE IT STALLS: three systems hold the same curve list and are synchronized by forms and emails, so curves go missing from V@R ("numerous curves in ERMS that are not in RisktRAC"). RAR has to spend time on a weekly hunt.

CHANGE: Treat ERMS as the curve master. On creation of a new curve (name, commodity, region, publication name), a job creates the matching RisktRAC curve and TAGG curve entry, or queues them for one-click approval by RAR and the TAGG admin. A nightly exception report lists any ERMS curve missing in RisktRAC or TAGG, replacing the weekly manual review.

AFTERWARDS: The risk manager creates the curve once. No forms or TAGG emails. RAR handles only exceptions from the nightly report.

ESTIMATE: (1) Weekly ERMS-vs-RisktRAC review by RAR, explicitly weekly in 410.eml, about 4.33 a month. Time is not stated; I assume a conservative 30 min to pull both curve lists, compare and chase owners, versus about 5 min to read an automated exception list. 25 min × 4.33 ≈ 108 min/month. (2) Per new curve: about 10 min for the risk manager to complete and send the RisktRAC form and the TAGG request email, plus about 10 min for RAR and the TAGG admin to key it, so about 20 min, versus about 2 min with one-click approval. The archive shows West desk requests on 19 Oct and 7 Dec 2000 (five curves), so I assume only 2 requests a month firm-wide (conservative, since 410.eml went to about 30 risk leads across all commodities): 2 × 18 = 36 min. Total ≈ 144 min ≈ 2.4 h/month × $85 ≈ $204/month.

49	Prihoda/HOU/EES@EES, Louis Colarusso/NYC/MGUSA@MGUSA, Christian 
50	LeBroc/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Rebecca Miller, Jan-Erland Bekeng/AP/Enron@Enron, 
51	Heidi Mason/ENRON_DEVELOPMENT@ENRON_DEVELOPMENT, David Port/Market 
52	Risk/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Vladimir Gorny/HOU/ECT@ECT, Frank 
53	Hayden/Corp/Enron@Enron, Bjorn Haglemann, Debbie R Brackett/HOU/ECT@ECT
54	cc: Sally Beck/HOU/ECT@ECT, Brent A Price/HOU/ECT@ECT, Mike 
55	Jordan/LON/ECT@ECT, Chris Abel/HOU/ECT@ECT, Susan D Trevino/HOU/ECT@ECT, 
56	Burton McIntyre/HOU/ECT@ECT 
57	Subject: requests for new curves, new books, porfolio changes
58	
59	In the past few months, the procedures for setting up new curves and books 
60	have not been followed by everyone. 
61	
62	The following memo documents the procedures to 1) set up a new curve, 2) set 
63	up a new book, and 3) change a portfolio hierarchy.  Please note that risk 
64	management (for each commodity group), "risk management"  is responsible for 
65	ensuring that information is flowing appropriately between the valuation 
66	systems and RisktRAC (Risk Analysis and Reporting can help, but do not have 
67	all of the ERMS information to be able to ensure the completeness of 
68	RisktRAC).
69	
70	I have attached the request form for each of these changes at the bottom of 
71	this memo.  Please ensure that everyone in your group obtains a copy. 
72	
73	The procedure to set up a new curve is as follows:
74	
75	Trader starts trading at a new location or a new commodity and needs a new 
76	curve set up
77	Trader communicates this to risk management
78	Risk management constructs new curve in ERMS (with the help of the IT 
79	department)
80	Risk management completes a curve set up request form to set up curve in 
81	RisktRAC
82	Curve form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
83	Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up curve in RisktRAC
84	A system generated message is sent to people on the "curve list" indicating a 
85	change in the RisktRAC curves has been made
86	
87	If the curve is not set up in RisktRAC the positions are not captured in the 
88	VAR or engine, thereby making VAR inaccurate.  As a side note, Risk Analysis 
89	and Reporting has implemented a new process in which on a weekly basis new 
90	curves set up in ERMS are reviewed to ensure that these have been set up in 
91	RisktRAC.  We did this for the first time today and noted numerous curves in 
92	ERMS that are not in RisktRAC - which we are working with you to resolve.
93	
94	The procedure to set up a new book in RisktRAC is as follows:
95	
96	Trader/risk management determines new book is needed
97	New book request form (for RisktRAC) is completed by risk management
98	New book request form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
99	Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up book in RisktRAC
100	Risk Analysis and Reporting forwards request to ERMS administrator and global 
101	counterparty group to request that book is set up in valuation and 
102	counterparty systems
103	Once all groups have completed their individual set ups, a final e-mail is 
104	sent to personnel on the "books list" and the book administrator in the risk 
105	management department who requested the book
106	
107	It is important that there is a one to one link between the ERMS and RisktRAC 
108	books, or not all positions will be captured in RisktRAC (two commodities per 
109	ERMS book does not flow properly into RisktRAC).
110	
111	The above two processes have formally existed for a number of months.  
112	Additionally, we are formalizing the procedure for changing portfolio 
113	hierarchies.  The procedure now is:
114	
115	Risk management is responsible for requesting all portfolio hierarchy 
116	changes.  Previously, changes could be made through a request by Risk 
117	Analysis and Reporting or RAC.  These two groups are no longer allowed to 
118	submit change requests.  All requests must come through risk management.
119	Risk management completes a request, including the reason for the requested 
120	change in structure
121	Risk management forwards the request to Risk Analysis and Reporting
122	Risk Analysis and Reporting makes the change and notifies risk management 
123	that the change has been made.
124	
125	If you have any questions, comments or concerns, please call: me X39123, 
126	Chris Abel X33012, Burton McIntyre X57197, or Susan Trevino X31462.
127	
128	Thanks,
129	
130	Shona

1	# Saved
2	
3	1. Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA: Meter the remaining service generators automatically so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls. ($3,102.50 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/335.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/357.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/506.eml
4	2. Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests: Produce a month-end file of each counterparty's official MTM by region, so Confirmations can answer period-end audit requests itself without asking the desks. ($1,381.25 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/137.eml, giron-d/sent/214.eml, giron-d/sent/240.eml, giron-d/sent/241.eml
5	3. Month-end basis and index roll-off in the gas risk books: Make the roll-off a scheduled setting in the risk calc, so one run produces both the 100% TDS view and the rolled V@R view. ($467.50 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/442.eml, giron-d/sent/631.eml
6	4. Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals: Book deals with every ECC counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically and send a daily list of any that slip through, instead of a monthly search of all books. ($364.65 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/108.eml, giron-d/sent/114.eml, giron-d/sent/195.eml, giron-d/sent/292.eml, giron-d/sent/360.eml, giron-d/sent/407.eml, giron-d/sent/535.eml, giron-d/sent/550.eml
7	5. Overriding MIPS zero volumes in POPS by hand: Have the MIPS nightly file mark 'no data yet' as incomplete instead of zero, so POPS keeps Gas Control's estimate and schedulers stop overriding zeros by hand. ($306.85 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/1013.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1014.eml, farmer-d/logistics/925.eml, farmer-d/logistics/928.eml, farmer-d/logistics/936.eml
8	6. Nightly El Paso (EPE) model vs. CARP reconciliation entry: Have a scheduled job compare the El Paso model with the CARP report each night, log the totals and a 'no variance' stamp itself, and flag only the variances for the trader. ($215.90 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/304.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/315.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/417.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/418.eml
9	7. Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen: After each month-end, a scheduled job copies the existing P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for every gas book into one package for Arthur Andersen, so the monthly request, forward and gather cycle stops. ($184.45 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/201.eml, giron-d/sent/299.eml, giron-d/sent/326.eml, giron-d/sent/327.eml, giron-d/sent/420.eml, giron-d/sent/515.eml, giron-d/sent/516.eml, giron-d/sent/583.eml
10	8. Nightly check that every book and post ID is marked official: Have the risk system email each book administrator and controller, every evening, the list of their post IDs not yet marked official, including flat ones. ($184.45 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/401.eml, giron-d/sent/492.eml, giron-d/sent/533.eml, giron-d/sent/580.eml, giron-d/sent/582.eml, giron-d/sent/595.eml
11	9. Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX: Turn on Access's automatic compaction for WeaponX so book admins no longer compact it by hand each week. ($147.05 a month). Cites giron-d/inbox/128.eml, giron-d/sent/585.eml, giron-d/sent/596.eml
12	10. Monthly EWS admin-assistant roster check: Build the roster each month from HR and phone-directory data instead of asking every assistant to check a spreadsheet. ($134.30 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/313.eml
13	11. Weekly California Capacity Report: Have the weekly California Capacity Report built and emailed automatically from flow and price data, with the marketer only checking it. ($88.40 a month). Cites lokay-m/inbox/10.eml, lokay-m/inbox/32.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/110.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/117.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/131.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/146.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/18.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/30.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/40.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/46.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/47.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/55.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/63.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/67.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/79.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/86.eml, lokay-m/sent_items/97.eml
14	12. Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets: Book the GLO swap once as term deals with a zero-price GLO sale and formula-priced demand tickets, so the only monthly input is the crude value. ($55.25 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/175.eml, farmer-d/logistics/28.eml, farmer-d/logistics/83.eml
15	13. Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets: Have Sitara roll each pipe's transport usage ticket into the next month automatically and fill its rate from the rate matrix, so staff key only the exceptions. ($53.55 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1796.eml, farmer-d/logistics/2109.eml, farmer-d/logistics/2111.eml, farmer-d/logistics/867.eml

HL&P month-to-date flow report: Have the system build and send the HL&P nominated-versus-actual month-to-date report every day, with short days flagged, instead of a scheduler updating and emailing a spreadsheet by hand each week. Why: The only evidence is one launch memo (86.eml, 19 Nov 2001), sent two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy and the desk's move to UBS Warburg on new systems, so nothing shows the 27 nightly Enpower confirmations, or the one-minute save, lasting long enough to save 13.5 hours a month; the full minute counted as lost is also not shown, and another critic already rejected this same nightly checkout work on the same evidence. Research that could settle it: Find messages from December 2001 onward (Enron estate or UBS Warburg Energy) showing the Real Time desk still confirming paths in Enpower Path Confirmation with many counterparties each night, and any complaint or note about the save time, to show the work and the wait continued.
63	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale as a standing zero-price ticket and price the HPL-to-ENA demand tickets by formula (firm volume x the month's index), so only the crude value is keyed monthly.. Why: The same change to the same work is already saved in decisions.md (item 7). This version also gets today's process wrong: the mail shows the monthly steps were not done at all from March 2001 on and had to be caught up months later, not keyed by hand each month before flash.
64	- Redirecting mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams: Have IT add department and location to both Bill Williams directory names so senders can tell them apart when addressing.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Correcting mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams' (item 8 in decisions.md), which uses 9 of this proposal's 16 occurrences, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
65	- Monthly auditor requests for gas P&L top pages and curve shift reports: At month-end, copy every book's daily P&L top pages and curve shift reports into one read-only audit folder that the auditors pull from themselves.. Why: This is already saved as item 4 in decisions.md ('Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen'), which cites the same eight messages and makes the same change, so saving it again would count the savings twice.
66	- Supplying P&L top pages and curve shift reports for Arthur Andersen's monthly gas testing: Each month-end, file the official P&L top pages and curve shift reports for every gas book in a read-only folder that AA can open, so AA stops asking the desks for them.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as item 4 in decisions.md, 'Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen', which cites all of this proposal's messages (201, 299, 326, 327, 420, 515, 516, 583), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
67	- Monthly repricing of EnerVest deal S#27239: Let Settlements set the invoiced price on deal S#27239 when it processes the EnerVest invoice, instead of emailing Risk to do it each month.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 14 in decisions.md, 'Monthly repricing of invoice-priced Sitara deals (27239 EnerVest, 27253)', which cites all six of these messages and proposes the same change.
68	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas/crude swap deal tickets: Book the GLO sale at zero price permanently and make the HPL-ENA and ENA-EGM demand tickets evergreen with formula amounts, so the only monthly input is the crude value.. Why: decisions.md already has the same work and the same change saved (item 9, $55.25 a month), and the mail shows the swap ran only from January to May 2001, so it was a short episode, not ongoing monthly work.
69	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude intercompany tickets: Set up the GLO/EGM intercompany legs as standing deals whose demand charges are calculated each month, with a check before flash, instead of zeroing prices and keying tickets by hand.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 10 in decisions.md, 'Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets' ($55.25 a month), which cites the same messages (175.eml, 83.eml, 28.eml), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
70	- Researching HPLC-ENA intercompany accrual variances: Have Sitara create the mirror side of every HPLC-ENA intercompany deal automatically, and add a daily intercompany nomination tie-out. Why: The mail shows an intercompany deal is already one shared Sitara deal (868: 'Intercompany Sitara deals are the same'); the missing sides are unmatched nominations and accruals, not missing deal tickets, so auto-creating mirror tickets would not remove them, and the claim that monthly recurrence is shown rests on one month's list. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how the ENA side of an intercompany Sitara deal gets nominated and why it goes missing (the 'system limitation' Lenart asks about in 868), plus intercompany variance lists for other months, to support a proposal built only on a daily nomination tie-out.
71	- Daily forwarding of the Energy Market Report to West traders: Have the report go straight to a West-traders distribution list, so nobody forwards it by hand.. Why: The same work and change is already saved as decision 17 ("Daily forward of the Energy Market Report to West Power traders"), which cites all seven of these messages, so saving it again would count the same saving twice.
72	- Monthly roll-forward of Texas desk transport usage tickets in Sitara: Have Sitara roll transport usage tickets into each new month by itself, with rates taken from the rate table used for invoicing, so accounting only reviews a list of gaps.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 11 in decisions.md (Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets), citing the same messages.
73	- Monthly roll of Texas transport usage tickets: Let Sitara transport usage tickets run for the whole contract term, take their rates from the rate matrix automatically, and carry last month's volumes forward.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets', which cites the same messages (1144, 1145, 1257, 1796, 2109, 2111, 867).
74	- Monthly repricing of EnerVest Sitara deal S#27239: Let the monthly EnerVest price be set without an email to the risk desk: either model the deal's real pricing in Sitara, or let settlements enter it with the desk reviewing afterwards.. Why: This work is already saved in decisions.md as item 17, 'Monthly repricing of invoice-priced Sitara deals (27239 EnerVest, 27253)', which cites the same six messages and proposes the same change.
75	- Monthly EWS admin-assistant roster check: Build the monthly admin-assistant list from HR/directory data and ask assistants to reply only when their record changed or is blank.. Why: The same work and change are already saved in decisions.md as item 8, 'Monthly EWS admin-assistant roster check' ($134.30 a month), which cites the same single message, williams-w3/sent_items/313.eml, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
76	- Daily hand-forwarding of the Energy Market Report to West power traders: Send the vendor's daily report straight to a distribution list of the 12 traders, or forward it with an automatic mail rule, so nobody forwards it by hand.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 19 in decisions.md, 'Daily forward of the Energy Market Report to West Power traders' ($8.50 a month), which cites all seven of these messages, so saving it again would count the saving twice.
77	- Monthly P&L support for Arthur Andersen gas testing: Save each gas book's month-end P&L top page, five largest-day top pages and curve-shift reports to a dated folder AA can read, so nobody pulls them on request.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 5 in decisions.md, 'Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen', which cites the same eight messages, so saving this would count the saving twice.
78	- Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration Report: Have the contract system produce the report on a fixed date before each bid week and email it to a list people join or leave themselves, so Cheryl only checks it.. Why: The same work is already saved in decisions.md as item 13, with the same change and the same messages (farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, 2114.eml), so saving it again would count it twice.
79	- ENA/Burlington capacity-release 50/50 marketing-fee split on TW billing: Configure TW billing to compute ENA's release credit and TW's marketing fee for contract 24924 automatically each month. Why: The mail shows a single one-off deal on one contract, seen for two months (a release effective 1/11/02 - 1/31/02 and then February), with no sign it continues; building custom billing logic for it would cost more than the roughly $71 a month it saves, and the part that actually stalls (whether TW pays ENA its half while ENA owes TW money) is a judgment call that billing logic cannot settle. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing that this release, or other releases with fee-sharing terms, ran for many more months or across several shippers, and for anything saying how CBS handles such terms; if neither exists, the verdict stands.
80	- Monthly Investor Relations volumetric explanations: Have the Statistical Database flag the +/-10% variances, show EOL and counterparty drivers, pre-fill last month's explanation, and collect the controllers' explanations in the database instead of by email.. Why: The change depends on things the mail does not show: that the Statistical Database holds EOL and counterparty detail, and that it does not already show the variances. The minutes are also inflated: 11 controllers' work is costed from one controller's two-line reply, and 11 readings are counted for a verifier who was copied only because one controller chose to copy him. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what the Statistical Database contains (variance columns, EOL or counterparty breakdowns), replies from controllers other than Baumbach, and other months' requests, and use them to show how long the explanations take and whether they repeat; then cost only the steps the change really removes.
81	- Monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations: Pre-fill each region's previous explanation next to every +/-10% variance in the Statistical Database, so controllers tick 'same driver' or type a new one there instead of replying by email.. Why: The same work was already rejected in decisions.md for the same gaps, and this version repeats them: 11 controllers' time is costed from one controller's (Baumbach's) one- and three-line replies, 'answers repeat' rests on one region in two months, and the change drops the stated rule that 'the volumes be verified by commercial personnel' for repeated drivers. Research that could settle it: Find replies from controllers other than Baumbach and requests for other months, showing how long the explanations take and whether drivers really repeat across regions; then cost only the steps the change removes (email reply and BA&R consolidation) and keep the commercial verification of volumes every month.
82	- Monthly gas curve-validation questions: Send each month's curve-validation questions straight to the owning trader from a maintained curve-owner list, and validate derived curves such as NGI-PGE/TOPOCK through their parent curve.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as item 15 in decisions.md ('Monthly gas curve validation questions', $28.05 a month), citing the same messages 132, 170, 47 and 49. This version also gets the facts wrong: only the January round went through Gossett and three leads. February and March went straight to the leads and then to Giron alone. TOPOCK was flagged only once. And the March re-ask came back unchanged even after Giron asked the trader directly.
83	- Nightly counterparty checkouts in Enpower Path Confirmation, Portland Real Time desk: Pre-fill counterparty contact details and make the Path Confirmation save run in the background, one batch per counterparty.. Why: The only evidence is one memo launching the tool (86.eml, 19 Nov 2001), sent two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy while counterparties were already stopping trades with Enron; nothing shows 25 counterparties being confirmed every night for long, the one minute of contact typing and the retyping of the same contacts are made up, and this same work and change were already rejected in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find messages from December 2001 onward (Enron estate or UBS Warburg Energy) showing the Real Time desk still confirming many counterparties' paths in Enpower Path Confirmation each night, with any note on save time or contact entry.
84	- Settling Real Time CAISO congestion-relief revenue: Take congestion revenue straight from CAPS finals into the daily flash, with an automatic exception list against the inc sheet, instead of trader emails, hand calculations and month-end true-up chases. Why: Most of the claimed saving rests on misreadings: the largest item (the desk's daily exposure tally, 150 of 370 minutes) is a net-position check the manager asked for and the change would not replace; Jim's hand calculation in 90.eml was a stopgap while the system was down ('When the system comes up'), and he says Volume Management 'haven't missed it for a long time'; the mail shows about 2 events a month, not 4; and once these are corrected, the added daily review of the exception list cancels most of what remains. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that congestion revenue is routinely left out of the flash month after month (true-ups like 266.eml beyond August 2001), and for how long Volume Management actually spends on each event when the system is up, to see whether a narrower check of the flash against CAPS saves real time.
85	- Transwestern short-term contract-quantity changes: Shippers submit one-day or few-day MDQ increases and month-to-month continuations on a web form; the marketer approves with one click and the contract system generates the amendment.. Why: The rate is not supported: all six distinct requests fall in 10-31 Dec 2001, and Lokay's sent mail from January to late March 2002 (about 100 messages) has none, so 6 a month is a one-month burst projected forward. The 15-minute amendment step is also assumed, and the marketer mostly forwards a one-word 'Approved.' rather than retyping terms. Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ or continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, Lindberg, Lohman, Y'Barbo, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Admin spends on a one-day amendment.
86	- Second, unposted TW Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the TW team once whether anyone uses Rita Bianchi's second Current Shipper rate matrix and stop keeping it up if nobody does.. Why: The work shows up only once in the archive (29 Oct 2001), and nothing says how often the Current Shipper rates change, so the quarterly or monthly rate behind the saving is a guess. Research that could settle it: Look for other TW rate-matrix postings or Current Shipper rate changes, such as earlier MATRIX*.doc files, Global Settlement surcharge updates, or Rita Bianchi's or Elizabeth Brown's mail, that show how often the rates change; and for any reply saying whether anyone uses the spreadsheet.
87	- Transwestern shippers' short-term contract change requests: Shippers send MDQ increases and month-to-month continuations through a structured request; the account director approves with one click and the system produces the amendment for contract admin to check.. Why: The rate of 8-9 a month comes from a three-week burst (10 Dec 2001 - 3 Jan 2002): Lokay's sent mail runs from 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and holds only about 10 such requests in all, about 2 a month, so at the proposal's own 15 minutes the saving is roughly 30 minutes a month, too little to pay for a shipper web form; the 15-minute amendment step is also assumed, and the same work was already rejected for this reason (decisions.md Rejected item 83). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, extension or continuation requests in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell) outside December 2001, and anything showing how long Contract Admin spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
88	- Weekly purchase-requisition processing by Mary Poorman: Move requisitions to SAP purchasing self-service with automatic approval routing and a named backup, so the coordinator handles only exceptions.. Why: The only evidence is one offhand remark in a message of doubtful origin (482.eml) that says nothing about the steps, volume or tools of the requisition work, so neither the SAP self-service fix nor the 10-hours-a-week saving can be shown from the mail. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows the requisition work happening: requisitions sent to or by Poorman, approval chases, purchasing or SAP requisition system mail, counts per week, and where the time goes. Confirm the message's origin against normal mail as well.
89	- Next-day long/short position notices to the Real Time shift: Replace typed 'Short/Long/Length for <day>' emails with an automatic next-day open-position view from Enpower that the shift checks at shift start. Why: The mail shows Real Time can already read these positions in Enpower (120.eml, 'according to Enpower, STNW is long on peak @ PGE System'), and the emails exist to carry what Enpower does not hold: deals booked only in CAPS (512.eml, 112.eml 'built in Caps but not in enpower', with Bill telling them to hold the Enpower deal until the next day), which deal number to link, and where to deliver or sell (120.eml, 172.eml), so the proposed view would not remove the notices. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that the notices mostly repeat data already correct in Enpower and carry no delivery or CAPS-only information; if so, a narrower change, such as a required template or a check against Enpower before sending (Kate's suggestion in 120.eml), might be proposed instead.
90	- Transwestern shippers' short-term capacity changes: Shippers submit one- or two-day MDQ increases, extensions and month-to-month continuations as a standard electronic request; the marketer click-approves and the system generates the amendment and updates the admin contract.. Why: The rate of about 8 a month comes from a three-week burst (10-31 Dec 2001) plus two long-term Red Rock receipt amendments (164.eml, 57.eml) that are not short-term changes; Lokay's sent mail runs 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and shows no short-term request after 3 Jan 2002, so the real rate is about 1-2 a month, and the same work has already been rejected twice for this reason (decisions.md Rejected items 83 and 85). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, one-day extension or monthly continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Administration spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
91	- Wellhead spot and interim tickets re-keyed in Sitara by logistics: Producer Services enter spot and interim baseload wellhead tickets in Sitara themselves instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The mail does not show that Producer Services can or do enter deals in Sitara (they ask others to enter even the committed-reserves tickets), the one correction cited was the requester's own typo that the change would not prevent, and the 12-a-month volume is about four times what the archive shows. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Producer Services staff entering deals in Sitara themselves, and whether deal entry is kept with logistics or deal-entry staff as a control; then count the actual spot and interim tickets requested per month across the whole year.
92

SAVED as 7 of 24 in decisions.md: 33 minutes x 4.33 times a month = 2.38 hours = $202.30 a month.
How often, counted: 2 gaps between its 3 times over the 3 months from 2000-10 to 2000-12, since the work is ongoing = 0.67 a month. A message and the replies that quote it are one time; the 3 occurrences given came to 3 times.
How often, stated: 1 a week = 4.33 a month. The stated rate is used, as the larger.

content.text:
I saved the proposal. It is item 7 of 24 in `decisions.md`, at 33 minutes × 4.33 times a month, which comes to 2.38 hours or **$202.30 a month**. That is in line with your $204.

**The claims match the mail:**
- **410.eml:** Shona Wilson's 22 Nov 2000 memo went to about 30 recipients. Susan Trevino forwarded it to Giron, and Giron forwarded it to Anne Bike. It lays out the steps for a new curve: the risk manager builds it in ERMS, fills in a request form, the form goes to Risk Analysis and Reporting, and they key it into RisktRAC. It also says a missing curve leaves positions out of V@R. It confirms the new weekly review of ERMS against RisktRAC, which on its first run found "numerous curves" missing.
- **TAGG requests:** 573.eml (19 Oct) asks Jeremy Wong to add curves to TAGG, and 569.eml has his "Done." reply. 411.eml (7 Dec) asks the same for three West curves.
- **No duplicate:** nothing saved or rejected in `decisions.md` covers this work. I also found no further TAGG curve requests in the mail beyond these.

**What I changed in the written proposal:**
- **Wong's role:** the mail never calls Jeremy Wong the "TAGG administrator". The proposal now just describes him as the person asked to add curves to TAGG.
- **One rate instead of two:** the check takes a single frequency per proposal, so I folded your two parts into one weekly figure. The 25 minutes saved on the weekly review plus your two new curves a month (36 minutes, about 8 per week) gives about 33 minutes a week, using the weekly rate stated in 410.eml.

How often curves are created is still your estimate. The mail shows only the West desk's two requests.

Files are in C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2:
- proposals\erms-curve-sync.json
- decisions.md

input.description: Monthly new-book-codes check for NYMEX invoicing
input.prompt:
Proposal: Give Gas Settlements an automatic month-end list of books that newly hold third-party financial deals, instead of Settlements calling and emailing the risk leads each month before running NYMEX invoices

TODAY: Before the month-end NYMEX invoice run, Settlements (Rebecca Ford's group, Beatrice Reyna) asks the risk leads by phone or email whether any books are new or have just started holding third-party financial deals. The question cascades down the risk hierarchy, and books are still missed.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/556.eml, Rebecca Ford, 15 Aug 2000: "During the August settlement period, we discovered at least 4 book codes that had just recently started containing financial, third-party deals in them.  We tried to put a procedure into place where we were calling the risk guys to find out about new books.  I don't know, however, if we are calling the right people because we were not told about the 4 books that we discovered on our own." / "From now on, I am going to have Beatrice Reyna from my group call someone from Reporting (Frank) and key people in Risk before we run our NYMEX invoices at the end of the month." / "Even if the book codes are not brand new, but if they have just started putting financial deals in them, WE NEED TO KNOW ABOUT THEM."
- The same file shows the October 2000 round. Beatrice Reyna, 26 Oct, to Keiser, Gossett and Baumbach: "Does anybody have any new book codes?  Also, if anyone knows who Kyle Etter's replacement is, please let me know." Gossett forwards to William Kelly and Darron Giron, and Giron replies: "You can start asking me about the West desk.  We don't have any new books for this month." The contact list also had to be rebuilt by hand ("Kyle Etter, East / Kam Keiser, Central / Jeff Gossett, West / David Baumbach, Texas").
WHERE IT STALLS: it depends on Settlements knowing whom to ask as people change (Etter's replacement), and on each lead remembering new books. In August 4 books were missed and had to be found by Settlements on its own.

CHANGE: A month-end query on the risk/deal system (TAGG/ERMS book and deal tables) lists every book code that has third-party financial deals settling in the invoice month and that did not have them the prior month, plus any newly created book codes. It is emailed automatically to Settlements before the NYMEX invoice run. Risk leads look at it only if Settlements has a question.

AFTERWARDS: No monthly call or email round, no cascade through Gossett, and no contact list to maintain. Books that newly carry financial deals are caught by data, not memory.

ESTIMATE: Frequency is monthly: "before we run our NYMEX invoices at the end of the month" (556.eml). Per month today: Reyna's emails and calls to about 4 regional leads plus Reporting, about 10 min. Each of about 5 risk leads checks their books and replies or forwards (the October round went Reyna → Keiser/Gossett/Baumbach → Gossett → Kelly/Giron), about 5 min each = 25 min. Reyna compiles and follows up, about 10 min. Total about 45 min. Afterwards about 5 min to review the automatic list, so about 40 min saved a month ≈ 0.67 h × $85 ≈ $57/month. I do not count the cost of the missed books or re-invoicing, which the mail does not quantify.

2	  "name": "Setting up new forward curves in RisktRAC and TAGG",
3	  "today": "A desk risk manager builds a new curve in ERMS. To get it into the V@R system (RisktRAC) the risk manager fills in a paper curve set-up request form and sends it to Risk Analysis and Reporting (RAR), who key it into RisktRAC. Separately, the risk manager emails Jeremy Wong to add the curve to TAGG, and waits for his reply. Steps get skipped: RAR found 'numerous curves in ERMS that are not in RisktRAC', which leaves positions out of V@R. RAR now checks ERMS against RisktRAC by hand every week to catch the gaps.",
4	  "change": "Set up each new ERMS curve in RisktRAC and TAGG automatically and report any gaps nightly, instead of request forms, emails and a weekly manual check.",
5	  "explanation": "Treat ERMS as the master list of curves. When a risk manager creates a curve in ERMS, a job creates the matching curve in RisktRAC and in TAGG, or puts it in a queue for RAR and the TAGG administrator to approve with one click. A nightly report lists any ERMS curve still missing from RisktRAC or TAGG. Afterwards the risk manager creates the curve once and sends no form or email; RAR and the TAGG administrator only handle the items on the exception report, and RAR no longer runs its weekly comparison by hand.",

Each month at Seven Oaks, TECO (PG&E) makes an adjustment to the allocation 
to either pay HPLC for underages or charge HPLC for overtakes - ie. the 
difference between what our producers put in the plant and what we take from 
the plant after shrinkage.  This adjustment arrangement doesn't seem to be 
papered - it's just occurred each month for the past 5 years on a relatively 
routine basis.

Since the adjustment arrangement isn't papered, we've been having difficulty 
properly reflecting the deal in sitara and unify.  It has been suggested that 
we try to paper the deal for posterity (the lease to TECO has 9 more years to 
run), but, in view of the forthcoming expiration of the primary term of both 
the Comstock and Oryx (Sun and/or Kerr-McGee) contracts, I'm reluctant to 
open this can of worms.  I'd like your thoughts.

George x3-6992

29	Subject: Teco's Indian Spring Plant
30	
31	A meeting was held on November 1, 2000 at 3 pm in EB3270 to resolve Exxon's 
32	residue volume issue at Teco's Indian Spring Plant.   Exxon's issue is that 
33	the residue volumes that HPL is recording for Exxon's account for 
34	transportation do not equal to the wellhead volumes produced and delivered to 
35	PGE.   
36	
37	Items that were identified so that Exxon's Issue could be resolved:
38	
39	 1.  HPL is responsible for any UA4 loss/gain and fuel consumed on PGE's line 
40	attributable to Exxon's Big Sandy production.
41	 2.  If Exxon's production exceeds 500 mcf/d, HPL must on a monthly basis 
42	elect to process or not process the Exxon Big Sandy Gas.  If HPL elects 
43	to       process, then Teco buys the products from HPL.
44	 3.  If Exxon's production flows between 100 Mcf/d and 499 Mcf/d, then Teco 
45	can process and makeup the shrinkage to HPL with their own gas volumes. 
46	 4.  If Exxon's production is less than 100 Mcf/d, then HPL must terminate 
47	the Processing Agreement.  If HPL does not terminate and volume continue 
48	to        flow at less that 100 Mcf/d than HPL loses the shrinkage and must 
49	pay to Teco an additional $500 per month.
50	
51	Solution:
52	 1.  HPL will schedule and record the Gain/Loss Volumes at HPL Meter #986884 
53	that is attributable to UA4 and Fuel on the PGE line.
54	 2.  HPL will schedule and record the sale volumes of PVR to Teco at HPL 
55	Meter #986884. 
56	 3.  The scheduling of the volumes for items  1 and 2 will allow for offset 
57	volumes to be record as adjustments to Exxon's transport volumes.
58	 4.  The HPL Logistics dept. (Mary Poorman) will inform Assets Group (Jack 
59	Simunek) when and if the volumes nominated for Exxon fall below 100 Mcf/d.
60	
61	If any of the above does not reflect what was discussed or agreed to, please 
62	let me know at X-36650.
63	
64	Thanks, Clem
65

Clem Cernosek@ECT

To: Sherlyn Schumack/HOU/ECT@ECT, Lauri A Allen/HOU/ECT@ECT, Jack 
Simunek/HOU/ECT@ECT, Karry Kendall/HOU/ECT@ECT, Mary Poorman/NA/Enron@Enron, 
Howard B Camp/HOU/ECT@ECT, Katherine Herrera/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Megan 
Parker/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Jennifer D Pattison/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc: Rita Wynne/HOU/ECT@ECT, Pat Clynes/Corp/Enron@ENRON 

Subject: Teco's Indian Spring Plant

A meeting was held on November 1, 2000 at 3 pm in EB3270 to resolve Exxon's 
residue volume issue at Teco's Indian Spring Plant.   Exxon's issue is that 
the residue volumes that HPL is recording for Exxon's account for 
transportation do not equal to the wellhead volumes produced and delivered to 
PGE.   

Items that were identified so that Exxon's Issue could be resolved:

 1.  HPL is responsible for any UA4 loss/gain and fuel consumed on PGE's line 
attributable to Exxon's Big Sandy production.
 2.  If Exxon's production exceeds 500 mcf/d, HPL must on a monthly basis 
elect to process or not process the Exxon Big Sandy Gas.  If HPL elects 
to       process, then Teco buys the products from HPL.
 3.  If Exxon's production flows between 100 Mcf/d and 499 Mcf/d, then Teco 
can process and makeup the shrinkage to HPL with their own gas volumes. 
 4.  If Exxon's production is less than 100 Mcf/d, then HPL must terminate 
the Processing Agreement.  If HPL does not terminate and volume continue 
to        flow at less that 100 Mcf/d than HPL loses the shrinkage and must 
pay to Teco an additional $500 per month.

Solution:
 1.  HPL will schedule and record the Gain/Loss Volumes at HPL Meter #986884 
that is attributable to UA4 and Fuel on the PGE line.
 2.  HPL will schedule and record the sale volumes of PVR to Teco at HPL 
Meter #986884. 
 3.  The scheduling of the volumes for items  1 and 2 will allow for offset 
volumes to be record as adjustments to Exxon's transport volumes.
 4.  The HPL Logistics dept. (Mary Poorman) will inform Assets Group (Jack 
Simunek) when and if the volumes nominated for Exxon fall below 100 Mcf/d.

If any of the above does not reflect what was discussed or agreed to, please 
let me know at X-36650.

Thanks, Clem

content.text:
I saved the proposal as item 22 of 27 in `decisions.md`. The saving is 20 minutes a month, about $28 a month, which is lower than the proposal's figure of 40 minutes and $57.

**What holds up.** The idea is sound and the evidence supports it. In `corpus/giron-d/sent/556.eml`, Rebecca Ford sets up a standing month-end check "before we run our NYMEX invoices at the end of the month." She says the calls missed at least 4 books, which Settlements then found on its own. The October round in the same file shows the check happening: Reyna asks the leads and also asks who replaced Kyle Etter, Gossett forwards the question to Kelly and Giron, and Giron replies. Nothing like this is already saved; the only nearby saved item is about repricing EnerVest deals, which is different work.

**What I changed:**
- **Minutes, from 40 to 20.** The October round was quick: a one-line question, one forward, and a "no new books" reply, all within about 40 minutes. Nothing in the mail shows each lead spending 5 minutes checking their books. I estimated about 25 minutes for the round today (Reyna's calls and emails, short replies from about 5 leads, the forward, Reyna's follow-up), less about 5 minutes to review the automatic list.
- **The system named.** The proposal said the report would run on "TAGG/ERMS book and deal tables," but this thread never names a system. ERMS does appear elsewhere in the same mailbox, so I wrote "the risk system's book and deal data (for example ERMS)" so as not to claim something the mail doesn't show.
- **How often.** The quote for the monthly rate is now "invoices at the end of the month," because the words used before didn't say how often.

**Remaining weakness.** The work appears in only one thread, so "monthly" rests on Ford's stated plan, with one round actually seen (October). As before, the saving leaves out the cost of missing a book and having to re-invoice, since the mail doesn't put a figure on it.

The saved file is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2\proposals\new-financial-book-codes.json`.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Paper the Seven Oaks / meter 986884 plant gain-loss adjustment with Teco (now El Paso / PG&E) once as an evergreen buy/sell, with standing Sitara purchase and sale deals at the meter, so Volume Management can allocate and draft each month without chasing logistics, the trader and settlements for deal numbers

TODAY: Each month the processing plant operator at Seven Oaks (meter 986884) allocates an adjustment that makes HPL either a buyer or a seller. The arrangement was never papered, so the Sitara buy/sell deals keep expiring or becoming unusable. Each month Volume Management parks the volume on Strangers Gas, or cannot draft it, and emails around for deal numbers or extensions.
- Explicit frequency, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1626.eml (George Weissman, 29 Mar 2000): "Each month at Seven Oaks, TECO (PG&E) makes an adjustment to the allocation to either pay HPLC for underages or charge HPLC for overtakes - ie. the difference between what our producers put in the plant and what we take from the plant after shrinkage.  This adjustment arrangement doesn't seem to be papered - it's just occurred each month for the past 5 years on a relatively routine basis." / "Since the adjustment arrangement isn't papered, we've been having difficulty properly reflecting the deal in sitara and unify." / "(the lease to TECO has 9 more years to run)". The same file, Thu Nguyen (22 Jun 2000): "I need to have the purchase from (Teco) and sale to (Teco) deals in order to allocate correctly.  For May 00, we are purchasing from Teco.  I am allocating this to strangers gas at moment".
- January 2001 production, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2099.eml (23 Feb 2001), a four-person chain (Schumack → Olsen → Parker → Herrera → Farmer). Sherlyn Schumack: "Have you heard anything about extending the buy/sell ticket for TECO yet?   Today is the last day we can make changes in the system." Michael Olsen: "I was unable to extend the deal for Teco # 137870 and #235670 becaus e it has been suspended.  Teco is no longer the counterparty." Katherine Herrera: "Do we have the buy/Sell deal for El Paso ( formerly Teco)  for January 01 Prod?" And corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2095.eml: "Volume management was wondering if deals 137870 and 235670 needed to be extended into 2001." / "Teco Gas Processing Company is suspended. / Deal with inactive or suspended counterparty may not be extended."
- February 2001 production, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2150.eml (4 Apr 2001), Katherine Herrera: "This deal has expired for Teco Gas Processing, but we did have a sale in 02/01. / Should this deal be extended?" / "Unable to draft volume in Unify due to the expired deal ticket;". Julie Meyers: "Daren, did we purchase gas for meter 6884 for February?"
- December 2000, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2067.eml: Mary Poorman: "PG&E has allocated an offsetting sale at the meter to TECO, and claim that they are net deals.  I do not show a sale in the system at the meter". It ran from 22 Jan to 1 Feb 2001 through Schumack, Simunek and Gottlob ("we have a purchase booked here, we need to reverse?").
- The arrangement is also the agreed recording point for Exxon gain/loss and PVR sales: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1503.eml (Nov 2000): "HPL will schedule and record the Gain/Loss Volumes at HPL Meter #986884" / "HPL will schedule and record the sale volumes of PVR to Teco at HPL Meter #986884."
WHERE IT STALLS: no paper and no standing deals. Every month's allocation needs someone to find or extend deals, and the counterparty change (Teco → El Paso) blocked extensions at the system's change deadline.

CHANGE: Execute a short buy/sell (gain/loss) agreement with El Paso, the successor to Teco, for meter 986884 covering the lease term. Set up evergreen purchase and sale Sitara deals at the meter, priced per the agreement and under the current counterparty name. Volume Management allocates the monthly adjustment to them directly. The trader gets an FYI only if the volume is unusual.

AFTERWARDS: No monthly "do we have the buy/sell deal" emails, no strangers-gas parking, no blocked extensions or missed drafting deadlines.

ESTIMATE: Frequency is monthly ("Each month", 1626.eml). People per month today, per the January 2001 chain: Volume Management (Schumack) asks about 5 min; logistics (Olsen) checks and tries to extend about 10 min; settlements (Parker, Herrera) forward and ask about 10 min; the trader (Farmer, Meyers) researches whether gas was bought or sold about 10 min; the accounting arrangement or strangers-gas re-allocation about 10 min. Total about 45 min. Afterwards about 5 min to glance at the allocation, so about 40 min saved a month ≈ 0.67 h × $85 ≈ $57/month. Larger one-off clean-ups such as December 2000 (2067.eml) are not counted.

Fred or Anita,

 I just wanted to recap our discussion to be sure that we are all on the same 
page.  From my understanding, the allocation for meter 785: State Tract 121 
is supplied from Bryancy Braumley.  Prior to 09/1/00 Bryancy would calculate 
flow from certain wellheads, total this volume, and then send us an 
allocation that would show how much gas was allocated to Texas General Land 
and HPL (Sale from CLECO) at meter 785.  Effective 09/1/00 a compressor was 
put in and the gas from 785 now flows through this compressor, as well as the 
gas from meter 9662 (Deal 137595 Sales from Dewbre), and is now measured at 
meter 3527:Tivoli Station.  For Bryancy's allocation, she must take the meter 
statement from meter 3527 and deduct meter 9662's flow.  Once this is done, 
she can take that net number and do an allocation between Texas General Land 
and HPL (CLECO) like she has done previously.  I believe meter 785 is now a 
check meter and meter 3527 is the actual pay meter.

 For 9/00 there were two deals in place for the sale from CLECO, deal 397957 
and 449243.  Per discussions with Daren Farmer, Danny Conner, and Jennifer 
Martinez, I have been instructed to zero out the deal for 397957 and use 
449243 as the correct deal number.  Therefore, Fred Boas and I have zeroed 
out the 397957 deal and placed the volume that was allocated there to deal 
449243.  Deal 397957 was priced at ship less .18 which was incorrect and deal 
449243 is priced at ship less .15.  Therefore, an adjustment will generate 
for 9/00 for the difference in price and the change in location.  The 
allocated volume for CLECO did not change.  However, I am not sure that 
Bryancy is allocating the volume properly between Texas General Land and HPL 
(CLECO).  I have spoke to her, as well as Jennifer Martinez, and Curtis 
Funderbruk with CLECO so there might be some PMA's for volume differences.  
In addition, I have changed the allocation method at meter 3527 to be a 
callout\swing effect 9/00.  For October and succeeding months, the volume 
should be computed by taking meter 3527 deducting out meter 9662.  Then 
Byancy should take this net number and split it between Texas General Land 
and HPL (CLECO).  The Texas General Land nom is currently at meter 785 and 
the HPL (Cleco) deal is at meter 3527.  Fred mentioned that the Texas General 
Land nom might need to be moved to meter 3527 but nothing has been decided on 
that yet.  

 Please let me know if something I have stated is not your understanding or 
you need something more done on my end.  Also, let me know who is going to be 
doing this monthly allocation.  It might be beneficial to have one person 
doing all the points (meters 3527, 9662, 785).  Thanks for your help!!!

24	Simunek/HOU/ECT@ECT, Karry Kendall/HOU/ECT@ECT, Mary Poorman/NA/Enron@Enron,

26	Parker/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Jennifer D Pattison/HOU/ECT@ECT
27	cc: Rita Wynne/HOU/ECT@ECT, Pat Clynes/Corp/Enron@ENRON 
28	
29	Subject: Teco's Indian Spring Plant
30	
31	A meeting was held on November 1, 2000 at 3 pm in EB3270 to resolve Exxon's 
32	residue volume issue at Teco's Indian Spring Plant.   Exxon's issue is that 
33	the residue volumes that HPL is recording for Exxon's account for 
34	transportation do not equal to the wellhead volumes produced and delivered to 
35	PGE.   
36	
37	Items that were identified so that Exxon's Issue could be resolved:
38	
39	 1.  HPL is responsible for any UA4 loss/gain and fuel consumed on PGE's line 
40	attributable to Exxon's Big Sandy production.
41	 2.  If Exxon's production exceeds 500 mcf/d, HPL must on a monthly basis 
42	elect to process or not process the Exxon Big Sandy Gas.  If HPL elects 
43	to       process, then Teco buys the products from HPL.
44	 3.  If Exxon's production flows between 100 Mcf/d and 499 Mcf/d, then Teco 
45	can process and makeup the shrinkage to HPL with their own gas volumes. 
46	 4.  If Exxon's production is less than 100 Mcf/d, then HPL must terminate 
47	the Processing Agreement.  If HPL does not terminate and volume continue 
48	to        flow at less that 100 Mcf/d than HPL loses the shrinkage and must 
49	pay to Teco an additional $500 per month.
50	
51	Solution:
52	 1.  HPL will schedule and record the Gain/Loss Volumes at HPL Meter #986884 
53	that is attributable to UA4 and Fuel on the PGE line.
54	 2.  HPL will schedule and record the sale volumes of PVR to Teco at HPL 
55	Meter #986884. 
56	 3.  The scheduling of the volumes for items  1 and 2 will allow for offset 
57	volumes to be record as adjustments to Exxon's transport volumes.
58	 4.  The HPL Logistics dept. (Mary Poorman) will inform Assets Group (Jack 
59	Simunek) when and if the volumes nominated for Exxon fall below 100 Mcf/d.
60	
61	If any of the above does not reflect what was discussed or agreed to, please 
62	let me know at X-36650.
63	
64	Thanks, Clem
65
