Tim,

Probably 3 to 5 months ago David Poston demonstrated a new position manager=
 to work with both FSP and Enpower. David Poston showed the position manage=
r to me, Cara Semperger, and Phil Platter. Dave suggested that the new posi=
tion manager would replace the current stand-alone position managers in CAP=
S and Enpower. When Dave and I ran through the demonstration, I was told th=
at the East desk had driven most of the development work to date. The funct=
ionality of the position manager in the stage Dave presented to me seemed u=
seful, with little development needed for us to implement it. The position =
manager looked like it would offer several improvements over Real-Time's cu=
rrent position and report reconciliation methods. My impression of the appl=
ication was that it would be a portion of FSP when implemented and was not =
a stand alone application. Within a week after demostrating the new positio=
n manager, Dave relayed to me that production of the position manager would=
 be delayed until after FSP was in production. As a result of the FSP delay=
, I have heard nothing of the position manager and have had no input on it =
since that first meeting. I think this application (as I saw it last) has t=
he potential to improve our reports and reduce our time spent running them.=
 This application should be of benefit to preschedulers, risk and deal cont=
rol. Now that the position manager is back on the table, I would like the r=
eal-time group to be involved in the implementation of this portion of FSP =
and work to improve its ability to act as a report reconciliation tool.

If you have any questions please let me know.

Thanks,
Bill

Burton,
The following spreadsheets were still loaded from the ng_directory. Rock did 
call me saying that some pipe option spreadsheets were not loading through 
the new process and when I checked it seemed like a network problem and asked 
him to run it again and it seemed to be OK.

With the new process, there is no need for double quotes around the curve 
code and counterparty code columns anymore. This has been automatically taken 
care of since we process from the spreadsheet itself. This was the original 
problem around the pipe option spreadsheets which we discovered yesterday and 
the reason why the numbers did not match between the old and new processes.

I also noticed that INTRA-NORTHEAST-PHY was officialised 4 times - 2 times in 
a row in quick succcession.

I would like Rock or Robin to load these spreadsheets once again during the 
day with Virendra or me as early as possible. We have been consistently been 
able to load these into the test data bases.

The ng spreadsheet also has a quoted price curve code. It should not take any 
time to convert these spreadsheets over.

The ft_northwest sheet seems to be fine - just that it was put into the ng 
directory. Please advise them not to use this directory anymore. Any NT based 
directory will give much better response.

The surprises are the rll and the plastics text files. I thought these were 
the first to go the new spreadsheet format.

Brian Gillis was able to load his spreadsheets successfully through terminal 
server from Calgary yesterday.

Regards,
Ramesh

20	Group,
21	Enron is attempting to reconcile the daily activities of each counterparty with us. This includes when each counterparty cut us, and schedules that were moved. To facilitate these efforts please put all cuts and scheduling sheets in the accordion file on the RT overflow desk (where Kate used to sit).
22	
23	Also, stay tuned for new information on EPE. Apparently the information communicated by Tony was not completely correct.
24	
25	Thanks,
26	
27	Bill

X-From: Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=BWILLIA5>
X-To: Anderson, John </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Janders3>, Bland, Todd <Todd.Bland@ENRON.com>, Dean, Craig <Craig.Dean@ENRON.com>, Guzman, Mark </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mguzman3>, Meyers, Albert </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bmeyers>, Mier, Michael </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mmier>, Slinger, Ryan </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Rslinger>, Solberg, Geir </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Gsolber>, Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bwillia5>
X-cc: 
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \ExMerge - Williams III, Bill\Inbox
X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
X-FileName: 

Group,
Enron is attempting to reconcile the daily activities of each counterparty with us. This includes when each counterparty cut us, and schedules that were moved. To facilitate these efforts please put all cuts and scheduling sheets in the accordion file on the RT overflow desk (where Kate used to sit).

Also, stay tuned for new information on EPE. Apparently the information communicated by Tony was not completely correct.

Thanks,

Bill

Subject: EPE Hourly Deals 2002

Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
X-From: Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=BWILLIA5>
X-To: Anderson, John </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Janders3>, Bland, Todd <Todd.Bland@ENRON.com>, Dean, Craig <Craig.Dean@ENRON.com>, Guzman, Mark </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mguzman3>, Meyers, Albert </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bmeyers>, Mier, Michael </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mmier>, Slinger, Ryan </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Rslinger>, Solberg, Geir </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Gsolber>, Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bwillia5>
X-cc: 
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \ExMerge - Williams III, Bill\Inbox
X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
X-FileName: 

Group,

There is a new binder for EPE hourly deals for 2002. The deal sheets MUST be kept in this binder. We are currently missing the deal sheet for 12/30/01 to 01/01/02. Please be on the lookout for this sheet or sheets. Those who were on shift for that period will need to coordinate what deals were done and will need to reconstruct a sheet. 

These sheets are currently a main source of information on EPE for settlements. The deal sheets should be clear, concise, and should have information such as energy type, delivery point, who you spoke with and at what time.

I will be sending another email regarding EPE procedure and model updates for 2002.

Thanks,
Bill

17	Jim @ Kaztex bought 20/d NBPL @ Harper on our behalf from Tenaska.  Jim sold it to us at his cost, he said--$1.84.  Said yesterday's deal was at 2 cents over his cost, but that you had done him a favor and that he also owed us one related to something Patrice had done for him, so that 'we're even' now.  
18	Shelly @ MRT called to say that she wouldn't be needing the second package of 5000 for the weekend.  As you know, this set in motion quite the adventure.  
19	Reliant informed us that Domtar was not taking gas, and we had to get an additional 10/d for the weekend off their system.  Here's how we got rid of the 5 not taken by MRT and the 10 not taken by Domtar:
20	Sinha @ Aquila bought 3126 of North at 1.65.  Deal ticket #1182363.
21	Sylvia took the remaing 6874 of North, plus 5172 combined Flex & South and moved them to Laquiba (sp?) for sale to OG&E, incurring fuel of 1.3% plus $0.02 transport charge.  Sylvia sold the delivered volume of 11718 to OG&E for $1.85, deal ticket # 1182441.  Later in the day Reliant told us that we had been cut at Laquiba--only 2/d of flow there for the weekend, so we had to find another home for the remaining 9718/d.  Ended up taking the remainder to Enogex @ Chandler.  Souad handled the nominations; Bonnie was also involved in the gas control issues as well.
22	Spoke with Bonnie about the Domtar buyback ticket (Tammy was sick today).  Bonnie knew nothing about it.  Bonnie said that we needed to wait until she could see all of the deal tickets in Sitara.  Given Bonnie's and our lack of familarity with the Domtar provisions, we decided to wait until Monday to enter the Domtar side of the deal with your assistance.
23	Melinda @ MidAm called to get our offer on 50 contracts of the Dec-Aug NYMEX swap.  Dutch quoted at $0.35, with $2.82 on the front.  Melinda held off.  Spoke wiht her later and she said that she'd gotten done elsewhere 'at a different price'.
24	Cheryl @ Terra bought our remaining 3193 of OGT at $1.59.  Deal ticket #1182379.  Sinha, ever the bottom-feeder, had earlier bid us $1.59 when our offer was $1.69.  Denver was showing the OGT at $1.60 when Cheryl called, but he was eager to get rid of it, so he jumped at the $1.59.  No unpleasant calls from Credit as of 2:30pm.
25	Greg Hayes @ Farmland called for an offer of 2000/d of Demarc for the weekend.  He could see Denver's 10/d offered on EOL, but explained that he was calling because he only wanted 2/d.  Asked Denver if he would do 2/d, and Denver suggested that I remind Greg that he could adjust his buy quantity on EOL.  Denver verbally quoted $1.72.  Went back to the phone and communicated our offer of $1.72 to Greg.  Greg asked if he could have it at $1.70, as that was the price that was showing on EOL at the beginning of our conversation, he claimed.  Ran this past Denver, but Denver stood fast at $1.72.  Greg did not sound happy and asked for my name and number.  Haven't heard anything further.
26	Sinha called again at about 9:50 and asked if we had 1800 PEPL to sell him.  Denver was done for the day, so no deal.  
27	
28	
29	Please don't hesitate to ask me if you need some further clarification on any of this.  I'll be reachable by cell over the holiday weekend at 713-213-7644.  
30	
31	Hope you and your family are having a nice Thanksgiving.  Sorry that we had to pull you away for such an extended period this morning.
32	
33	
34	Patrick
35

corpus\farmer-d\logistics\1294.eml:124:customer attempts a transaction, the database must "lock" each and every

90	- Transwestern short-term contract-quantity changes: Shippers submit one-day or few-day MDQ increases and month-to-month continuations on a web form; the marketer approves with one click and the contract system generates the amendment.. Why: The rate is not supported: all six distinct requests fall in 10-31 Dec 2001, and Lokay's sent mail from January to late March 2002 (about 100 messages) has none, so 6 a month is a one-month burst projected forward. The 15-minute amendment step is also assumed, and the marketer mostly forwards a one-word 'Approved.' rather than retyping terms. Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ or continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, Lindberg, Lohman, Y'Barbo, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Admin spends on a one-day amendment.
91	- Second, unposted TW Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the TW team once whether anyone uses Rita Bianchi's second Current Shipper rate matrix and stop keeping it up if nobody does.. Why: The work shows up only once in the archive (29 Oct 2001), and nothing says how often the Current Shipper rates change, so the quarterly or monthly rate behind the saving is a guess. Research that could settle it: Look for other TW rate-matrix postings or Current Shipper rate changes, such as earlier MATRIX*.doc files, Global Settlement surcharge updates, or Rita Bianchi's or Elizabeth Brown's mail, that show how often the rates change; and for any reply saying whether anyone uses the spreadsheet.
92	- Transwestern shippers' short-term contract change requests: Shippers send MDQ increases and month-to-month continuations through a structured request; the account director approves with one click and the system produces the amendment for contract admin to check.. Why: The rate of 8-9 a month comes from a three-week burst (10 Dec 2001 - 3 Jan 2002): Lokay's sent mail runs from 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and holds only about 10 such requests in all, about 2 a month, so at the proposal's own 15 minutes the saving is roughly 30 minutes a month, too little to pay for a shipper web form; the 15-minute amendment step is also assumed, and the same work was already rejected for this reason (decisions.md Rejected item 83). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, extension or continuation requests in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell) outside December 2001, and anything showing how long Contract Admin spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
93	- Weekly purchase-requisition processing by Mary Poorman: Move requisitions to SAP purchasing self-service with automatic approval routing and a named backup, so the coordinator handles only exceptions.. Why: The only evidence is one offhand remark in a message of doubtful origin (482.eml) that says nothing about the steps, volume or tools of the requisition work, so neither the SAP self-service fix nor the 10-hours-a-week saving can be shown from the mail. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows the requisition work happening: requisitions sent to or by Poorman, approval chases, purchasing or SAP requisition system mail, counts per week, and where the time goes. Confirm the message's origin against normal mail as well.
94	- Next-day long/short position notices to the Real Time shift: Replace typed 'Short/Long/Length for <day>' emails with an automatic next-day open-position view from Enpower that the shift checks at shift start. Why: The mail shows Real Time can already read these positions in Enpower (120.eml, 'according to Enpower, STNW is long on peak @ PGE System'), and the emails exist to carry what Enpower does not hold: deals booked only in CAPS (512.eml, 112.eml 'built in Caps but not in enpower', with Bill telling them to hold the Enpower deal until the next day), which deal number to link, and where to deliver or sell (120.eml, 172.eml), so the proposed view would not remove the notices. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that the notices mostly repeat data already correct in Enpower and carry no delivery or CAPS-only information; if so, a narrower change, such as a required template or a check against Enpower before sending (Kate's suggestion in 120.eml), might be proposed instead.
95	- Transwestern shippers' short-term capacity changes: Shippers submit one- or two-day MDQ increases, extensions and month-to-month continuations as a standard electronic request; the marketer click-approves and the system generates the amendment and updates the admin contract.. Why: The rate of about 8 a month comes from a three-week burst (10-31 Dec 2001) plus two long-term Red Rock receipt amendments (164.eml, 57.eml) that are not short-term changes; Lokay's sent mail runs 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and shows no short-term request after 3 Jan 2002, so the real rate is about 1-2 a month, and the same work has already been rejected twice for this reason (decisions.md Rejected items 83 and 85). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, one-day extension or monthly continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Administration spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
96	- Wellhead spot and interim tickets re-keyed in Sitara by logistics: Producer Services enter spot and interim baseload wellhead tickets in Sitara themselves instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The mail does not show that Producer Services can or do enter deals in Sitara (they ask others to enter even the committed-reserves tickets), the one correction cited was the requester's own typo that the change would not prevent, and the 12-a-month volume is about four times what the archive shows. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Producer Services staff entering deals in Sitara themselves, and whether deal entry is kept with logistics or deal-entry staff as a control; then count the actual spot and interim tickets requested per month across the whole year.
97	- Producer Services wellhead purchase ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services keys spot and one-month wellhead purchase tickets into Sitara itself instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The proposal rests on Producer Services already entering committed-reserves tickets in Sitara, but the mail shows the opposite: they write those tickets up and ask for the Sitara number after someone else enters them (789.eml: "Please supply the sitara number once entered"; 694.eml: "We will generate a ticket to be entered into sitara ASAP"), so the change means giving deal-entry rights to a new group, which the mail gives no basis for, and the time saved is small and guessed. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services (Taylor, Smith, Reinhardt, Graves) entering deals in Sitara themselves, or saying why deal entry is held by logistics or deal capture (a control rule or system access), and for any statement of how long Tom Acton spends entering these tickets.
98	- Weekly check of ERMS curves against RisktRAC: A nightly automatic comparison of the ERMS and RisktRAC curve and book lists replaces the weekly manual review.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Setting up new forward curves in RisktRAC and TAGG', which cites the same message (giron-d/sent/410.eml) and already replaces the weekly manual check with a nightly gap report.
99	- Transwestern marketers' weekly bullets round: Replace Kim Watson's Friday email request for bullets with a shared bullets page each account director fills in, with no 'none' replies.. Why: The mail shows only two bullets rounds in all (Fri 8 Mar and Fri 22 Mar 2002), Lokay sent other mail on Fridays 1 Mar and 15 Mar with no bullets, so the weekly rate of 4.3 a month is not supported, and the main time saved (Watson assembling the replies into a summary) does not appear in the mail at all. Research that could settle it: Look in Kimberly Watson's or the other account directors' (Lindberg, Lohman, McConnell, Y'barbo) mailboxes for further 'Bullets' requests and replies, and for the summary Watson builds from them, to show how often the round really happens and what she does with the replies.
100	- Emailing dated curve files to JPMorgan: Send the dated curve file to JPMorgan automatically from the official curve close, to a fixed address list, instead of Darron Giron emailing it by hand. Why: The mail shows only two such sends, six weeks apart, among the 163 messages Giron sent in Dec 2000 and Jan 2001, so the claimed every-business-day frequency is unsupported; several other claims about how the work is done are not in the mail either. Research that could settle it: Look for more Giron-to-JPMorgan curve emails, or any message saying JPMorgan gets curves on a schedule (daily, weekly, under a contract), and for anything showing the work takes minutes or causes errors beyond the one 'Sorry wrong address' resend.
101	- Manager approval of small expense reports in Concur: Auto-approve expense reports under $100 in Concur, with the manager reviewing a monthly digest afterwards.. Why: The five approvals in 12 days were a one-time rush to clear expenses before the group left Enron's expense system for UBSW Energy, so the work ends and the monthly rate of 12 is not real; the whole archive shows only seven such reports. Research that could settle it: Look for this approval work, and how often it happens, under UBSW Energy's new expense process after the transaction closes; Enron's Concur/XMS approvals for this group stop there.
102	- HL&P month-to-date flow report and shortfall check: Have the system produce the HL&P daily nominated-versus-flowed report, with the 5% tolerance and buyback volumes worked out, instead of a hand-built spreadsheet emailed each week.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 16, 'HL&P month-to-date flow report', which cites all eleven of these update emails plus the 12/99 shortfall thread (683.eml) and the June 2000 resend (1217.eml).
103	- Setting up a new trading book across TAGG, Sitara, RisktRAC/ERMS, CPR and EOL: One routed new-book request form with status tracking and a single completion notice, instead of separate emails to each system's administrator. Why: The routed process already exists: Shona Wilson's memo (giron-d/sent/410.eml, Nov 2000) says one RisktRAC book request form goes to Risk Analysis and Reporting, which forwards it to the ERMS administrator and Global Counterparty and sends a final email to the books list, and says this process had 'formally existed for a number of months'; Giron's own requests from Oct 2000 on (557, 564, 491, 160) are single form submissions to Trevino/McIntyre, so the scattered emails cited come from mid-2000, when people were not following the process, not from how the work runs now. Research that could settle it: Only a new angle could revive it: mail from after Nov 2000 showing that book requests made through the single form still bounce, stall or need follow-up emails to CPR, EOL or Sitara administrators. The steps the form does not cover (the CPR region and EOL trader mapping) would then be a narrower proposal, with its own count of how often it happens.
104	- Settling HPL day/spot deal price and volume disputes: Sitara sends each counterparty a next-morning recap of the prior day's HPL day deals so price and volume mismatches are fixed at once, not at invoicing.. Why: The disputes are a post-sale cleanup: HPL passed to AEP from June 2001 (136.eml, 106.eml 'a deal from when we were at Enron'), every disputed deal is for Dec 2000 to May 2001 production, the earlier mail shows only about three such threads in all of 2000, and several cited threads are not day-deal disputes, so there is no ongoing work at 5 a month for a recap to prevent. Research that could settle it: Find disputes over day deals in Enron's own books after June 2001, outside HPL (for example ENA Texas or other desks' settlements mail), at a steady rate, plus evidence of whether those deals were already confirmed by Enron's Confirmations group; without that the verdict stands.
105	- Upkeep of TW's second, unposted Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the recipients once whether anyone uses the unposted matrix, and retire it if nobody does.. Why: The archive shows the second matrix being sent only once (29 Oct 2001), and no message says how often Current Shipper rates change, so there is no basis for how often the saving would happen. Research that could settle it: Look for other Current Shipper or Global Settlement rate changes, other TW rate matrix postings, or anything that gives a schedule for those changes (for example, in Rita Bianchi's, Elizabeth Brown's or Jeanette Doll's mail). Two or more dated sends, or a stated schedule, would give a rate.
106	- Building the daily El Paso Electric (EPE) preschedule/schedule sheet: Generate the daily EPE schedule sheet from e-tags and Enpower deals, check it automatically against EPE's dispatch, and phone only the counterparties on the exception list.. Why: The change depends on tag data the mail shows Enron does not get (52.eml: the missing tag did not list EPMIWE, and only EPE's dispatchers had it), the error rate of 8 days a month is about four times what the mail shows, the checkout-call part repeats work already rejected (decisions.md item 60), and 133.eml is a turbine-outage note, not a daily EPE file. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Enron could read every tag in EPE's control area (for example as EPE's agent on the tagging system) and that the tags exist when the day-ahead sheet is built; count the schedule errors in the EPE sheet over several months; and find anything saying how long preschedule spends building the sheet each day.
107	- Month-end basis and index roll-off calculated twice: Have the risk system produce the 100% basis view and the rolled-off V@R view from one calculation, using a month-end roll-off percentage set centrally.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 3, 'Month-end basis and index roll-off in the gas risk books', which cites the same two messages (giron-d/sent/631.eml and 442.eml) and proposes the same change.
108	- Monthly vacation round and out-of-office coverage notices in Energy Operations / HPL logistics: One shared absence calendar replacing the monthly vacation request round, plus a standing desk-coverage matrix so out-of-office notices go only to backups. Why: The vacation-round half is already saved (decision 24, same calendar, same files 954/1143/1282), and the coverage-notice half rests on miscounted notices and a change that would stop telling the people who need to know who to call. Research that could settle it: A coverage-only proposal would need many more distinct scheduler out-of-office notices across the year, and something in the mail showing that callers went to the wrong person or that notices took real effort to write or re-send. Without that, the savings stay a few minutes a month.

content.text:
I saved the proposal as item 21 in `decisions.md`. It saves an estimated 30 minutes a month, about $42.50 a month.

The quotes you cited all match the mail. I made three corrections before saving:

- **How often the chasing happens:** Your draft said Volume Management chases deals or parks the volume on strangers gas "each month." The mail says the plant adjustment happens each month, not the chasing. The chasing shows up for May 2000, December 2000, and January, February, April and May 2001. Strangers-gas parking appears only once, in May 2000.
- **New evidence:** Megan Parker's July 2001 request (`95.eml`) shows that even after a new El Paso deal (637225) existed, it still had to be extended month by month. She waited 3 to 20 July for logistics and then had to ask the trader. This supports standing deals better than a one-time rename to El Paso would.
- **Minutes:** I lowered them from 40 to 30. Your 45 minutes across five people is fair for a month that gets chased, but not every month does, so 30 is the average across all months. The check counted only 0.29 occurrences a month from the five dated threads, against the stated "each month." The stated rate was used, and with the 30-minute average I think it is realistic.

**Caveat:** In March 2000 George Weissman was reluctant to raise a written contract with Teco while other contracts were up for renewal. So I framed the written agreement as optional; the standing deals alone remove most of the chasing.

**Overlap check:** Saved item 20, "Requests to extend expired deals at flowing meters," is related but cites none of these meter-6884 messages. Its rule-based roll-forward would not handle a deal that switches between buying and selling, or a suspended counterparty. So this is not a duplicate.

The proposal file is at `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2\proposals\seven-oaks-meter-6884-buy-sell.json`

24	Friday 1/19/01 - Received a call from Sheila at Basin regarding a well which 
25	may be coming on this weekend (meter 9696).  Phone Lee in Gas Control 
26	regarding same.  Lee informed me that HPL would prefer that the volumes are 
27	not brought on until a field tech can pull a sample and verify that there are 
28	no liquids involved.  Lee further informed me that the same day to Tejas at 
29	Hardy was not in the system, and, per Gary Hanks, needed to be corrected.  
30	Lee informed me that the volumes were actually split 10M at Hardy/Tejas and 
31	10M at Lomax.  I went into Sitara and updated the deal ticket, pathed and 
32	nominated over to Pops.
33	
34	Saturday 1/20/01 - 8:30 am  Sean paged regarding the nomination at Dow 
35	Freeport, he was questioning the validity, as we do not often flow at this 
36	meter.  I checked and the nomination was good for Saturday's gas day.  Sean 
37	informed me that the Valero Refinery was up and down and would be going 
38	completely down on Sunday.
39	
40	10:00 am  - Sean called regarding Tejas LaPorte, meter 665.  Apparently, the 
41	meter had a confirmed volume of 20M and HPL/ENA had no deal at the meter.  
42	Checked in POPS and discovered that the deal was confirmed at 20M on a deal 
43	volume of zero.  Informed Sean that the Tejas volume was confirmed.  Also, 
44	per Sean Koch George West (meter 6722) had a nomination increase of 10M, 
45	which he wanted to confirm.
46	
47	Sunday 1/21/01  10:00 am  Sean paged regarding the Dow meter 1442, Pops still 
48	showed a confirmed voume of 10M which Dow and Oasis showed at zero for 
49	Sunday.  I  checked the system and confirmed that the meter was indeed at 
50	zero and phoned Sean back to confirm.  Checked on MTP Hardy, Sean informed me 
51	that we came in on rate for Saturday and that current meter activity looked 
52	good.

Group,
We have had some problems recently with the creation of HA finals, with SQL errors, and as a result we have not been able to run reports. If it is a weekend (or holiday), we first need to import DA finals and then create DA finals in CAPS. After this is done we can import HA finals, and create the HA report. If the boxes are not checked, the CISO may have missed publishing certain hours. Please look in the load zones to find what hour-ahead finals may not have been published, or where CAPS may have just missed pulling them in. Sometimes it helps to pull the missing hour-ahead finals in individually. Once all the finals are in the load zones and int. interchanges, you should be able to create the final report. Please give me a call if you have any questions.

Thanks,
Bill

content.text: Arthur Andersen also sends monthly requests for deal tickets, confirmations and forwards detail, which are separate from the saved P&L package. Sending that to the critic.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Give Arthur Andersen self-service, read-only retrieval of the deal ticket, confirmation and forwards detail for the deals it samples in its monthly gas testing (new-deal and origination testing), instead of emailing the desk head, who forwards to a book admin to assemble each package

This is distinct from saved item "Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen" (giron-d/sent 201, 299, 326, 327, 420, 515, 516, 583), which covers book-level P&L top pages and curve-shift reports. This proposal covers deal-level documents for sampled deals, from different messages.

TODAY: Each month AA picks individual new or originated deals from the Originations Report and new-deal lists and emails the West desk head (Darron Giron) for the deal ticket, confirmation and forwards detail. Giron forwards to a book admin, who pulls the TAGG ticket, gets the confirmation and runs forwards detail. Requests stall when the desk head is away.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/324.eml (16 Jan 2001), Mark Austin (AA): "As part of our monthly testing we review the Originations Report and identify items for which we would like to view additional documentation.  Could you please provide the deal ticket, confirmation, and applicable forwards detail for deal#EC3952.32?" Giron forwards to Chris Walker: "AA is all over me today.  Please get this for Mark."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/332.eml (12 Jan 2001), "December New Deals Request": "the following is a list of new deals that we have identified for further testing.  At your earliest convenience, could you please provide the applicable deal ticket and forwards details for these two deals?" forwarded to Chris Walker.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/120.eml: original request 14 Mar 2001: "As part of our monthly gas testing, could you please provide the deal ticket, confirmation, and forwards detail for Deal #QT5176 orignated on 2/23/01 in the GD-NEW book." AA chased 27 Mar: "Could you please let me know the status on this information as soon as possible?" Giron forwarded to Patrick Ryder on 28 Mar, and (corpus/giron-d/sent/91.eml) re-forwarded to Kristen Clause on 5 Apr.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/118.eml (28 Mar 2001), Giron to AA: "I appologize for the delay.  I was on vacation when you sent the first request and somehow didn't see it when I was going through a week's worth of emails  .  I have a person in my group getting the information together."
WHERE IT STALLS: every sampled deal needs a person to relay and a person to assemble documents that already exist in TAGG, the confirmation system and the risk system. One request took three weeks (14 Mar → 5 Apr) and two forwards.

CHANGE: Provide AA (or a Risk Controls liaison serving all desks) a read-only deal-document view keyed by deal number that returns the TAGG ticket print, the executed confirmation image and the forwards-detail report. AA pulls its sample itself. The desk is asked only when a document is missing.

AFTERWARDS: No desk-head forward, no book-admin assembly, no vacation-related stalls.

ESTIMATE: Frequency: two monthly test streams are stated ("monthly testing" of the Originations Report in 324.eml; "monthly gas testing" in 120.eml; plus the monthly new-deals request in 332.eml), so at least 2 requests a month to the West desk. Per request today: the desk head reads and forwards, about 3 min (plus re-forwards and an apology when it stalls); the book admin pulls the ticket, obtains the confirmation and runs forwards detail, about 20 min. Afterwards about 3 min of desk time for occasional gaps. Saving about 20 min per request × 2 = 40 min/month ≈ 0.67 h × $85 ≈ $57/month for the West desk alone. Other gas desks receive the same AA testing but are not counted. AA's own time is not counted.

20	ass if the deal is between Enovate and Oneok but is then flipped to EMW to 
21	manage.  There will be twice as many legs and the volumes will need to be

28	From: Richard Tomaski@ENRON on 02/21/2001 11:42 AM
29	To: James Simpson/HOU/ECT@ECT, Kevin Radous
30	cc: Gregg Penman, Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT, Mark Mixon, Kay 
31	Classen/NA/Enron@Enron, Lee Fascetti, Paul Burgener, hermannt@pecorp.com 
32	Subject: OneOK storage deal
33	
34	Enovate sold a virtual storage service to OneOk marketing.  
35	
36	Transaction parameters:
37	MSV = 500,000 mmbtu
38	Daily injection \ withdraw rights = 0-25,000
39	enovate's demand charge = $1.75 per MSV mmbtu
40	Commodity charges = none
41	Term: Apr01 - Mar02
42	Location: People's Citygate
43	
44	
45	
46	As we all know, our risk managment systems will not handle this kind of a 
47	transaction without al ot of manual manipulation. Below are my 
48	recommendations for booking this transaction.
49	
50	1.  enovate should book the expected usage pattern based on the current 
51	market curve with a zero price (and hedge, if the trader wants) in enovate's 
52	MTM risk books.  The trader should periodically adjust this usage pattern as 
53	market conditions change.  The negative fallout from this expected usage 
54	should be applied against the demand charge.
55	 
56	2. As Oneok actually withdraws or injects gas into the virtual storage, we 
57	should record the transaction in Sitara and adjust our expected usage deal.  
58	The trader can hedge this position financially, physically or may be able to 
59	use the PGL Hub.
60	
61	3. The demand charge should be booked in Tagg & Sitara and offset with 
62	financial annuity so we will not realize any MTM gain on the demand charge.  
63	We will adjust this financial annuity as losses are incurred.  Once the 
64	annuity is all used up, we will take all losses as incurred.  Any annuity 
65	amount left over at completion of the program will be taken as a gain at that 
66	time.
67	
68	4.  This deal will be managed in the EMW book eventhough the actual 
69	injections\withdraws will be recorded in the enovate book.  The enovate 
70	physcial book will be flat - in and out at a zero price.
71	
72	Cost of Carry should work in our favor unless they elect to go negative 
73	early.  All cash requirement should fall out in our EMW books.
74	
75	Jim will build a model to determine the expected usage and track his related 
76	hedges (This will be similar to what Lee has, but not as complicated)
77	
78	This is not intended to be a comprehensive description of how to book this 
79	transaction, only an outline what I believe should be reflected in our 
80	books.  Please forward any questions or comments to me.  Thanks.
81	
82	Richard

From: Richard Tomaski@ENRON on 02/21/2001 11:42 AM
To: James Simpson/HOU/ECT@ECT, Kevin Radous
cc: Gregg Penman, Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT, Mark Mixon, Kay 
Classen/NA/Enron@Enron, Lee Fascetti, Paul Burgener, hermannt@pecorp.com 
Subject: OneOK storage deal

Enovate sold a virtual storage service to OneOk marketing.  

Transaction parameters:
MSV = 500,000 mmbtu
Daily injection \ withdraw rights = 0-25,000
enovate's demand charge = $1.75 per MSV mmbtu
Commodity charges = none
Term: Apr01 - Mar02
Location: People's Citygate



As we all know, our risk managment systems will not handle this kind of a 
transaction without al ot of manual manipulation. Below are my 
recommendations for booking this transaction.

1.  enovate should book the expected usage pattern based on the current 
market curve with a zero price (and hedge, if the trader wants) in enovate's 
MTM risk books.  The trader should periodically adjust this usage pattern as 
market conditions change.  The negative fallout from this expected usage 
should be applied against the demand charge.
 
2. As Oneok actually withdraws or injects gas into the virtual storage, we 
should record the transaction in Sitara and adjust our expected usage deal.  
The trader can hedge this position financially, physically or may be able to 
use the PGL Hub.

3. The demand charge should be booked in Tagg & Sitara and offset with 
financial annuity so we will not realize any MTM gain on the demand charge.  
We will adjust this financial annuity as losses are incurred.  Once the 
annuity is all used up, we will take all losses as incurred.  Any annuity 
amount left over at completion of the program will be taken as a gain at that 
time.

4.  This deal will be managed in the EMW book eventhough the actual 
injections\withdraws will be recorded in the enovate book.  The enovate 
physcial book will be flat - in and out at a zero price.

Cost of Carry should work in our favor unless they elect to go negative 
early.  All cash requirement should fall out in our EMW books.

Jim will build a model to determine the expected usage and track his related 
hedges (This will be similar to what Lee has, but not as complicated)

This is not intended to be a comprehensive description of how to book this 
transaction, only an outline what I believe should be reflected in our 
books.  Please forward any questions or comments to me.  Thanks.

Richard

77:- Monthly GLO/EGM gas/crude swap deal tickets: Book the GLO sale at zero price permanently and make the HPL-ENA and ENA-EGM demand tickets evergreen with formula amounts, so the only monthly input is the crude value.. Why: decisions.md already has the same work and the same change saved (item 9, $55.25 a month), and the mail shows the swap ran only from January to May 2001, so it was a short episode, not ongoing monthly work.
79:[Omitted long matching line]
98:[Omitted long matching line]

- Gathering P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen's monthly gas testing: A month-end job saves every gas book's top pages and curve-shift reports into a dated read-only folder AA can open, with a list of each book's owner.. Why: Another critic saved the same work with essentially the same change while this one was being checked ('Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen', decisions.md Saved item 4, $184.45 a month), and it cites the same Giron messages 201, 299, 327, 420, 516 and 583.
- Supplying P&L top pages and curve shift reports for Arthur Andersen's monthly gas testing: Each month-end, file the official P&L top pages and curve shift reports for every gas book in a read-only folder that AA can open, so AA stops asking the desks for them.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as item 4 in decisions.md, 'Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen', which cites all of this proposal's messages (201, 299, 326, 327, 420, 515, 516, 583), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
- Researching HPLC-ENA intercompany accrual variances: Have Sitara create the mirror side of every HPLC-ENA intercompany deal automatically, and add a daily intercompany nomination tie-out. Why: The mail shows an intercompany deal is already one shared Sitara deal (868: 'Intercompany Sitara deals are the same'); the missing sides are unmatched nominations and accruals, not missing deal tickets, so auto-creating mirror tickets would not remove them, and the claim that monthly recurrence is shown rests on one month's list. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how the ENA side of an intercompany Sitara deal gets nominated and why it goes missing (the 'system limitation' Lenart asks about in 868), plus intercompany variance lists for other months, to support a proposal built only on a daily nomination tie-out.
- Next-day long/short position notices to the Real Time shift: Replace typed 'Short/Long/Length for <day>' emails with an automatic next-day open-position view from Enpower that the shift checks at shift start. Why: The mail shows Real Time can already read these positions in Enpower (120.eml, 'according to Enpower, STNW is long on peak @ PGE System'), and the emails exist to carry what Enpower does not hold: deals booked only in CAPS (512.eml, 112.eml 'built in Caps but not in enpower', with Bill telling them to hold the Enpower deal until the next day), which deal number to link, and where to deliver or sell (120.eml, 172.eml), so the proposed view would not remove the notices. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that the notices mostly repeat data already correct in Enpower and carry no delivery or CAPS-only information; if so, a narrower change, such as a required template or a check against Enpower before sending (Kate's suggestion in 120.eml), might be proposed instead.

X-From: Mary Poorman
X-To: Pat Clynes
X-cc: Robert Cotten, Vance L Taylor, Daren J Farmer, Cynthia Hakemack, Kristen J Hanson
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \Darren_Farmer_Dec2000\Notes Folders\Logistics
X-Origin: Farmer-D
X-FileName: dfarmer.nsf

Pat,

I have been working with Volume Management, Settlements, Vance, and Bob to 
clean up some prior period and prior-to-current month issues.  This process 
should result in a correction to booked profit/loss for Vance and the desk.  
This has brought to my attention that we have been paying some parties 
manually for volumes when deals are not correctly entered.  I would propose 
that Logistics be included in the communication of when checks are manually 
cut.  It would be especially beneficial if we tracked manual checks by 
counterparty, meter, and/or deal ticket id or price.  I feel that this will 
allow us to spot and resolve potential issues more effectively.

Please let me know what your thoughts are on this matter.  

Thank you for your time,

Mary

3	  "today": "A desk risk manager builds a new curve in ERMS. To get it into the V@R system (RisktRAC) the risk manager fills in a paper curve set-up request form and sends it to Risk Analysis and Reporting (RAR), who key it into RisktRAC. Separately, the risk manager emails Jeremy Wong to add the curve to TAGG, and waits for his reply. content.text:
I saved the proposal. It is item 24 of 33 in `decisions.md`, at 25 minutes once a month, or about $35.70 a month. It is not a duplicate. The saved item on P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen covers book-level reports. This one covers the ticket, confirmation and forwards detail for individual sampled deals, and none of its messages (120, 91, 118, 324, 332) are cited anywhere in `decisions.md`.

The idea held up. Everything below matches the mail: AA's requests, Giron's "AA is all over me today" forward to Chris Walker, his vacation apology, AA's chase on 27 March, and the forwards to Patrick Ryder on 28 March and Kristen Clause on 5 April. I rewrote the draft before saving to fix these points:

- **How often it happens.** The draft counted two monthly test streams by treating 324.eml and 120.eml as separate streams. They are both "Originations" requests, so they are the same stream. The new-deals request (332.eml) is a second kind of request, but no message says it is monthly. The mail shows three requests from January to March 2001. I used the one stated rate ("As part of our monthly testing", 324.eml), which is 1 a month.
- **Minutes per request.** I raised this from 20 to 25, because a request can cover more than one deal (332.eml asks for "these two deals").
- **Claims the mail doesn't support.** I removed the specific names of the deal and confirmation systems and the assumption that the confirmation exists as a scanned image. The change is now worded as a read-only lookup by deal number.
- **The three-week stall.** The draft said the 14 March request took three weeks. The mail only shows it was still being forwarded on 5 April, not when it was finished, so the proposal now says that.

The check's count from the dates in the mail came to 0.67 times a month, so it used the stated 1 a month. AA's own time and the other gas desks' requests are not counted.

The saved file is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-2\proposals\aa-deal-documents.json`.

content.content:
99	- Next-day long/short position notices to the Real Time shift: Replace typed 'Short/Long/Length for <day>' emails with an automatic next-day open-position view from Enpower that the shift checks at shift start. Why: The mail shows Real Time can already read these positions in Enpower (120.eml, 'according to Enpower, STNW is long on peak @ PGE System'), and the emails exist to carry what Enpower does not hold: deals booked only in CAPS (512.eml, 112.eml 'built in Caps but not in enpower', with Bill telling them to hold the Enpower deal until the next day), which deal number to link, and where to deliver or sell (120.eml, 172.eml), so the proposed view would not remove the notices. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that the notices mostly repeat data already correct in Enpower and carry no delivery or CAPS-only information; if so, a narrower change, such as a required template or a check against Enpower before sending (Kate's suggestion in 120.eml), might be proposed instead.
100	- Transwestern shippers' short-term capacity changes: Shippers submit one- or two-day MDQ increases, extensions and month-to-month continuations as a standard electronic request; the marketer click-approves and the system generates the amendment and updates the admin contract.. Why: The rate of about 8 a month comes from a three-week burst (10-31 Dec 2001) plus two long-term Red Rock receipt amendments (164.eml, 57.eml) that are not short-term changes; Lokay's sent mail runs 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and shows no short-term request after 3 Jan 2002, so the real rate is about 1-2 a month, and the same work has already been rejected twice for this reason (decisions.md Rejected items 83 and 85). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, one-day extension or monthly continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Administration spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
101	- Wellhead spot and interim tickets re-keyed in Sitara by logistics: Producer Services enter spot and interim baseload wellhead tickets in Sitara themselves instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The mail does not show that Producer Services can or do enter deals in Sitara (they ask others to enter even the committed-reserves tickets), the one correction cited was the requester's own typo that the change would not prevent, and the 12-a-month volume is about four times what the archive shows. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Producer Services staff entering deals in Sitara themselves, and whether deal entry is kept with logistics or deal-entry staff as a control; then count the actual spot and interim tickets requested per month across the whole year.
102	- Producer Services wellhead purchase ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services keys spot and one-month wellhead purchase tickets into Sitara itself instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The proposal rests on Producer Services already entering committed-reserves tickets in Sitara, but the mail shows the opposite: they write those tickets up and ask for the Sitara number after someone else enters them (789.eml: "Please supply the sitara number once entered"; 694.eml: "We will generate a ticket to be entered into sitara ASAP"), so the change means giving deal-entry rights to a new group, which the mail gives no basis for, and the time saved is small and guessed. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services (Taylor, Smith, Reinhardt, Graves) entering deals in Sitara themselves, or saying why deal entry is held by logistics or deal capture (a control rule or system access), and for any statement of how long Tom Acton spends entering these tickets.

- Next-day long/short position notices to the Real Time shift: Replace typed 'Short/Long/Length for <day>' emails with an automatic next-day open-position view from Enpower that the shift checks at shift start. Why: The mail shows Real Time can already read these positions in Enpower (120.eml, 'according to Enpower, STNW is long on peak @ PGE System'), and the emails exist to carry what Enpower does not hold: deals booked only in CAPS (512.eml, 112.eml 'built in Caps but not in enpower', with Bill telling them to hold the Enpower deal until the next day), which deal number to link, and where to deliver or sell (120.eml, 172.eml), so the proposed view would not remove the notices. Research that could settle it: Look for evidence that the notices mostly repeat data already correct in Enpower and carry no delivery or CAPS-only information; if so, a narrower change, such as a required template or a check against Enpower before sending (Kate's suggestion in 120.eml), might be proposed instead.
- Transwestern shippers' short-term capacity changes: Shippers submit one- or two-day MDQ increases, extensions and month-to-month continuations as a standard electronic request; the marketer click-approves and the system generates the amendment and updates the admin contract.. Why: The rate of about 8 a month comes from a three-week burst (10-31 Dec 2001) plus two long-term Red Rock receipt amendments (164.eml, 57.eml) that are not short-term changes; Lokay's sent mail runs 29 Oct 2001 to 25 Mar 2002 and shows no short-term request after 3 Jan 2002, so the real rate is about 1-2 a month, and the same work has already been rejected twice for this reason (decisions.md Rejected items 83 and 85). Research that could settle it: Find short-term MDQ, one-day extension or monthly continuation requests outside December 2001 in other TW marketers' or Contract Administration's mail (Dennis Lee, Michael Bodnar, TK Lohman, Paul Y'Barbo, Lindberg, McConnell), and anything showing how long Contract Administration spends on a one- or two-day amendment.
- Wellhead spot and interim tickets re-keyed in Sitara by logistics: Producer Services enter spot and interim baseload wellhead tickets in Sitara themselves instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The mail does not show that Producer Services can or do enter deals in Sitara (they ask others to enter even the committed-reserves tickets), the one correction cited was the requester's own typo that the change would not prevent, and the 12-a-month volume is about four times what the archive shows. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Producer Services staff entering deals in Sitara themselves, and whether deal entry is kept with logistics or deal-entry staff as a control; then count the actual spot and interim tickets requested per month across the whole year.
- Producer Services wellhead purchase ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services keys spot and one-month wellhead purchase tickets into Sitara itself instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The proposal rests on Producer Services already entering committed-reserves tickets in Sitara, but the mail shows the opposite: they write those tickets up and ask for the Sitara number after someone else enters them (789.eml: "Please supply the sitara number once entered"; 694.eml: "We will generate a ticket to be entered into sitara ASAP"), so the change means giving deal-entry rights to a new group, which the mail gives no basis for, and the time saved is small and guessed. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services (Taylor, Smith, Reinhardt, Graves) entering deals in Sitara themselves, or saying why deal entry is held by logistics or deal capture (a control rule or system access), and for any statement of how long Tom Acton spends entering these tickets.

I have a couple of questions regarding TGLO transport contract 
012-88494-202.  We are currently delivering a volume of 28.000mm into various 
Midcon interconnects on this contract that are designated to go to 
Reliant/Entex for the purpose of heating HISD schools.  The transport 
contract stipulates different rates for this delivery depending on whether 
the gas is intended for state facilities or not.  My first question, then, 
is:  are HISD schools considered state facilities?  And, if HISD schools are 
considered state facilities, does the fact that this gas is being delivered 
to them via Reliant/Entex utilizing Midcon's pipe make any difference?

I am asking these questions not only to assure that we are recouping the 
correct transport rate, but also to determine what the consequences might be 
if I interrupt this delivery.  We are having difficulty getting enough gas 
into Midcon to cover our Entex noms and I am just exploring my options.  I 
would also expect that this volume should decrease when HISD closes for the 
Christmas holidays- does the fact that this is an IT agreement give me enough 
leverage to cut this nom if TGLO does not do so voluntarily?

Thanks for your help.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Produce HPL's monthly industrial buyback/swing deal list as a scheduled Sitara report, instead of Julie Meyers compiling and emailing an updated spreadsheet to 13 people each month

TODAY: Each month Julie Meyers (deal entry) updates a spreadsheet of the industrial customers' buyback deals by hand and emails it to 13 people in logistics, volume management, settlements and the desk (Henn, Camp, Herod, Schwarz, Papayoti, Farmer, Lamphier, Hull, Seaman, Baumbach, Csikos, Ngo, Lloyd), asking them to forward it further. Allocation and settlement staff rely on it to know which buybacks are active.
- Explicit frequency, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/601.eml (Howard Camp, 20 Dec 1999): "the buyback issue is that  a buyback is set up until June 2000 per Julie Meyers notes she sends out every month ( Last note sent Dec  3 and you are on distribution list)." The same thread shows the list is the working reference when allocations are disputed: "Do we have an active buyback in place and how do you decide to use the buyback?" / "If not, please notify Julie and note on the deal ticket that this buyback is no longer effective."
- The monthly sends: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/650.eml (5 Jan 2000), "UPDATED SPREADSHEET": "Here is the lastest and greatest.  Please make sure that you look at this carefully.  There are some weird changes that happened.  PLEASE MAKE SURE THAT YOU FORWARD THIS ON TO WHOM EVER NEEDS IT." corpus/farmer-d/logistics/827.eml (22 Feb 2000), "FEBRUARY UPDATES": "Sorry so late." corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1078.eml (28 Apr 2000), "UPDATED SPREADSHEET": "Here are the updates for May.  You will notice I have not added the extra deals for Equistar Chemical because it didn't effect the whole month, plus I only found the split out for the sale upto 4/00 not the purchase."
- Related, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/645.eml (Kenneth Seaman, 4 Jan 2000), "Buyback Deals -- January 2000": "Attached are the current buyback deals I'm aware of. If you have further information please let me know."
WHERE IT STALLS: the list is assembled by searching deal tickets (1078.eml: "I only found the split out for the sale upto 4/00 not the purchase"). It arrives late (827.eml), depends on manual forwarding to whoever needs it (650.eml), and errors or omissions surface only in allocation disputes (601.eml).

CHANGE: Flag buyback and swing deals in Sitara with a buyback type and the linked base deal, as they are already entered as separate tickets: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/664.eml shows "Base 148376 / Swing 148382 / Buyback 148381". A scheduled month-start report lists each industrial meter's active base, swing and buyback deals with term and price, posted to a shared location or emailed to a self-maintained distribution list. Julie reviews it instead of building it.

AFTERWARDS: No hand-built monthly spreadsheet and no "forward to whoever needs it". Everyone sees the same current list on the first of the month.

ESTIMATE: Frequency is monthly ("notes she sends out every month", 601.eml). Today Julie researches the month's buyback deals and splits and updates the spreadsheet, about 45 min (the mail shows she searches tickets and still misses pieces), then sends and fields questions. Afterwards about 10 min of review. That saves about 35 min a month ≈ 0.58 h × $85 ≈ $50/month. Recipients' forwarding and reading time, and the cost of allocation disputes like 601.eml, are not counted.

	Enron North America Corp.
	
	From:  Heidi Withers                           03/02/2000 03:53 PM
	

To: Mary M Smith/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc:  
Subject: Re: transport flash for Feb 00  

The rates are in the system correctly in Unify (so that we can invoice 
correctly), but Daren's group uses a Sitara deal (the transport usage 
tickets) to estimate desk transport in the P&L during the month.  Right now 
we have not entered in or corrected rates in their transport usage tickets.  
Our group has not taken that step, since we have been most concerned with 
settling the G/L (after the month is over).  By not having the right rates on 
the transport usage tickets, the risk is that the P&L will be off during the 
month.  Would we change process and let Daren set up the transport usage 
ticket and then have us enter the rate?  If so, we would need to change the 
process with his group to put us in the process so that we can enter the 
correct rate.  Please let me know what you want to do.



Mary M Smith

To: Heidi Withers/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc: Lisa Hesse/HOU/ECT@ECT 
Subject: Re: transport flash for Feb 00  

Heidi, we need to ensure the rates are correct on all meters (HPLC/ENA for 
Texas) and that the rates are in the right system.


   
	Enron North America Corp.
	
	From:  Heidi Withers                           03/02/2000 10:34 AM
	

To: Mary M Smith/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc:  
Subject: transport flash for Feb 00

FYI...the economics group publishes this report every month to show how much 
the marketing desk spent in transport.  They can get their expense numbers 
either from their estimate (from CPR) or from Unify, where we put the rates 
in.

One potential enhancement would be that in addition to managing rates for the 
transport capacity tickets, we set up the rates for the transport usage 
tickets.  I am going through the transport usage tickets for February right 
now (as part of the market meter study) and I see some rates I don't tie back 
to Lauri's matrix.  For example, Lauri's matrix shows 0.05 from Thompsonville 
to HSC, but the transport usage ticket (updated by Daren's group) has 0.055.  
This means the economic estimate can be off.  Let me know what you want to do 
with this.
